**Amended in v1.12 (fifty-first cycle - the specification is re-derived from its own text by an independent implementation on a fresh pull, the parts that do not reproduce are superseded in place, the four conventions the text left open are fixed, the minimum detectable effect is written in as a closed form, and the registered statistic is required to be net of the funding carry; written after the re-derivation was executed and before any outcome measurement).** (i) **The counts the text fixes reproduce exactly on a fresh pull of both legs, by an implementation written from the plan of record's text alone.** The publisher's leg was pulled from the venue's USDⓈ-M monthly per-symbol funding-rate archive (81 months x 2 symbols; **7,395** settlements per symbol, 2020-01-01 00:00 to 2026-09-30 16:00; every row carrying `funding_interval_hours` = **8**; **no** two settlements falling in one 8-hour grid bucket; settlement jitter at most **47 ms**; **no** duplicate `calc_time`). The second venue's leg was pulled from its **legacy** per-instrument daily product (2021-01-01 to 2022-01-16, **381** files per instrument) and its **all-swap** daily product (2022-01-17 to 2026-10-20). Two structural facts about the second venue's leg were verified and are now binding: the legacy product's file for date D carries the three settlements of **D** at 00:00, 08:00 and 16:00, and its `real_funding_rate` at `funding_time` T equals the all-swap product's `funding_rate` at settlement instant **T minus 8 hours** on **93 of 93** compared instants with **0** mismatches - the forecast column mismatching on **93 of 93** - which confirms the plan's legacy-leg offset and its column choice by measurement. Under the plan's own rules this reproduces **4,037** matched settlements inside the window, **3,767** eligible, **738** trigger settlements for BTC (**348** upper, **390** lower) and **734** for ETH (**338** upper, **396** lower), **310** and **303** merged episodes, **180** independent 5-day windows for both instruments, and **58** and **56** independent 20-day windows. The entry's arithmetic is therefore correct and reproducible; what is not reproducible is the specification that is supposed to produce it.

(ii) **The window's end is now stated, and it is load-bearing.** Every recorded count is conditional on the window **2022-01-01 00:00 UTC to 2025-09-08 00:00 UTC (exclusive)** - the last matched settlement is 2025-09-07 16:00 UTC - and the plan did not state it, so no third party could have reproduced the counts from the text. The end is where the second venue's **legacy** product stops being published (its last file is 2025-09-07), and the **all-swap** product has continued past it: on 2026-10-21 the all-swap daily tree carries files for **299 of the last 300 days**, to **2026-10-20**. The recorded window is therefore a **pull boundary and not a pre-registered end date**, and the plan now says so and states the date. The cost of the alternative is stated so that a validator can see it: extending the window to the end of the available data (last matched settlement 2026-09-30 16:00 UTC) gives **5,201** in-window matched settlements, **4,931** eligible, **997** and **993** trigger settlements, **413** and **408** episodes, **238** and **243** independent 5-day windows and **76** and **74** independent 20-day windows for BTC and ETH - so the choice is worth roughly **+30%** on the binding number, in the direction of more power.

(iii) **The independent-window rule is fixed, because the text as written does not produce the recorded numbers.** The v1.11 clause (g) says independent forward windows "are counted from the first eligible observation at or after the previous window's end". Read literally over the eligible **settlement** series, that gives **270** windows at 5 days and **68** at 20 days - **50% and 17% more** than the recorded **180** and **58**/**56**, and those are the numbers the entry's effective-sample bound and its minimum detectable effect are built on. The recorded numbers reproduce under one rule and one only: **each trigger settlement opens a forward window, and the next window opens at the first trigger settlement at or after the previous window's end.** The plan now states that rule explicitly, and states again that the trigger count is not the binding number.

(iv) **The recorded counts that do not reproduce are superseded in place, and the cause is not asserted.** (a) "**5,201 matched settlements per instrument (4,037 inside the window)**" is not a possible pair: on a single pull the matched series has **6,297** grid points in total, of which **1,096** lie before the window start, **4,037** lie inside the window to 2025-09-08, and **5,201** lie inside the window if the window is extended to the end of the data. The two recorded numbers are counts on **two different pulls**, and the structure above replaces the pair. (b) "**761 pre-window matched settlements**" does not reproduce: the measured number is **1,096** (2020-12-31 16:00 through 2021-12-31 16:00 inclusive, 365 days x 3 + 1). (c) The alternative reading's numbers do not reproduce either: carrying the series back to 2020-12-31 16:00 gives **903** and **901** trigger settlements, **385** and **375** episodes, and **225**/**223** independent 5-day windows and **74**/**71** independent 20-day windows for BTC and ETH, against the recorded **779**/**775**, **333**/**325** and "**192 and 62** independent 20-day windows"; the recorded pair is also internally impossible, because **192** non-overlapping 20-day windows cannot fit in a 1,346-day window - the maximum is **67** - and 192 is a 5-day count. (d) The recorded slow-clock figures (**57** extreme weeks of **192** weekly observations and **36** independent 20-day windows for BTC; **65** and **39** for ETH) are not jointly reproducible: across **96** combinations of the four conventions the text leaves open - the daily aggregation (mean, first or last settlement of the day), the trailing window's alignment (the seven days ending on the sample day, or the seven preceding it), the weekly sampling phase (seven options) and the band's include/exclude rule (12 excluding the current observation, or 13 including it) - **no combination yields BTC (57, 36) and ETH (65, 39) together.** The measured values under the plan's stated band rule are in (v).

(v) **The slow clock's remaining conventions are fixed, and the BTC-versus-ETH difference is an artefact of the unstated conventions rather than a property of the instruments.** The plan now specifies: the **daily value is the mean of the day's matched pair differences**; the **trailing seven calendar days are the seven days preceding the sample day**, so that the sample's own settlement is not inside its own trailing mean; the sample is the **Monday 00:00 UTC** settlement; the band is the **12 weekly observations excluding the current observation** with linear-interpolated percentiles; and the 24-hour episode merge is **not** applied on the weekly clock, where consecutive extreme weeks are seven days apart and every extreme week is therefore its own episode. Under that reading the recorded window gives **191 weekly samples** (not 192), **60** extreme weeks for BTC and **64** for ETH, and **36 independent 20-day windows for both instruments**. The entry's recorded **39 for ETH against 36 for BTC therefore does not survive a single declared convention** - under one convention the two instruments give the *same* binding number, and what genuinely differs between them is the extreme-week count, which is an instrument difference rather than a specification artefact. The number is quoted only with the convention, and the convention is now in the plan.

(vi) **The minimum detectable effect is written into the plan of record as a closed form with the block structure declared, and the null's publishability condition is stated.** The thirty-sixth cycle required the MDE to be computed from the pre-registered window counts and the pre-registered block structure and reported in the units of the registered statistic; the forty-ninth cycle did not supply it. It is supplied here in the only form this repository can supply it without crossing its own scope boundary: **MDE = (t_{1-alpha/2, n-1} + t_{1-beta, n-1}) x SE_block**, two-sided **alpha = 0.05**, **power = 0.80**, the multiplier taken from the binding window counts - **2.8169** at n = 180 (5-day), **2.8504** at n = 58 and **2.8523** at n = 56 (20-day, instantaneous) and **2.8821** at n = 36 (20-day, slow clock) - where **SE_block** is the block-bootstrap standard error of the registered statistic, which the **validator** measures, in the units of the registered statistic (bp per week). The catalogue does not estimate SE_block here, because estimating it would require measuring the outcome series, which is empirical validation and outside this repository's scope; the MDE is therefore a **formula with declared constants**, and the entry's null clause now reads: the null may be reported as evidence of no effect only if the validator reports SE_block and the resulting MDE alongside it, and otherwise the null is reported as *uninformative* with the window counts stated alongside. The pre-registered block structure is **completed, not replaced**: on the instantaneous construction the block is the registered forward window itself (5 or 20 days), because the windows are non-overlapping by construction and the dispersion level's documented one-to-three-hour half-life is far shorter than the block; on the slow clock the block is a **moving block of at least four weekly observations (28 days)**, which covers the 20-day holding horizon and the weekly sampling cadence, with the sensitivity of SE_block to 2, 4 and 8 weekly blocks reported.

(vii) **The registered statistic must be net of the funding differential accrued over the forward window.** New in this cycle, from the claim side. The cross-venue funding spread is a **documented carry**, not only a signal: a June 2026 study of a cross-venue funding spread on perpetual futures reports a delta-neutral cross-venue dislocation earning roughly 7% annualised, significant into 2026, and reports that the single-venue carry is "a general phenomenon, present on every venue" (Lau, SSRN 6993978), while the peer-reviewed contract-design work documents that perpetual futures dominate crypto trading volume, enhance liquidity and reduce extreme price dislocations (Gornall, Rinaldi and Xiao, revised 2025-05-19). The entry's registered statistic is a **relative-return** difference between the expensive venue and the cheap venue, and the two venues are *defined* by their funding rates, so the funding differential is mechanically a large component of the difference over a 5- or 20-day window. A test that does not net it cannot distinguish the entry's registered mapping from the documented carry. The plan therefore requires the registered statistic to be reported **net of the funding differential accrued over the forward window** - equivalently, as a price-return difference with the funding accrual removed - with the gross figure reported alongside, and it requires the accrued differential to be computed on the same settlement grid as the signal. This is a construction amendment made in advance of any outcome measurement; it does not change what is claimed.

(viii) **None of this changes the registered prediction.** The sign of the venue-relative mapping remains untested and is not guessed; the registered measurement, the horizons, the comparator and the null are unchanged. The amendments make the measurement reproducible by a third party - which this cycle has demonstrated is not currently the case - and they complete the entry's effective-sample clause with the MDE formula the thirty-sixth cycle required. **No dimension moves and the total stays at 55** (12+3+6+15+3+8+8), for the reason recorded in item 16.

**Amended in v1.13 (fifty-second cycle - the fifty-first cycle's specification is audited by a second independent implementation on a second independent pull, a fifth unstated convention is found and fixed, the legacy product's row structure is corrected in place, the net-of-carry rule is made executable, the block structure and the null clause are completed, and the legacy vintage's whole count set is measured; written after the re-derivation was executed and before any outcome measurement).** (i) **Every number the fifty-first cycle superseded reproduces, on a pull made independently of the pull it was measured on, and the implementation is a different one.** Both legs were pulled again - the publisher's USDⓈ-M monthly per-symbol `fundingRate` archive (**81** months x 2 symbols; **7,395** settlements per symbol, 2020-01-01 00:00 to 2026-09-30 16:00; every row's `funding_interval_hours` = **8**; no two settlements in one 8-hour grid bucket; no duplicate `calc_time`) and the second venue's **legacy** per-instrument daily product (2021-01-01 to 2025-09-07, **1,711** files per instrument) and **all-swap** daily tree (2022-01-17 to 2026-10-20) - and the implementation was written from the plan of record's text alone, with the percentiles, the episode merge, the independent-window rule and the slow clock's conventions re-implemented from the v1.12 text rather than copied from the fifty-first cycle's code. It reproduces **6,297** matched grid points in total, **1,096** before the window start, **4,037** inside the window to 2025-09-08 and **5,201** inside the window if the window is extended to the end of the data; the alternative reading's **903**/**901** trigger settlements, **385**/**375** episodes, **225**/**223** independent 5-day windows and **74**/**71** independent 20-day windows; the window's own **4,037** matched, **3,767** eligible, **738**/**734** trigger settlements (**348**/**390** and **338**/**396**), **310**/**303** episodes, **180**/**180** at 5 days and **58**/**56** at 20 days; and the slow clock's **191** weekly samples, **60**/**64** extreme weeks and **36**/**36** independent 20-day windows. The four minimum-detectable-effect multipliers reproduce **to the digit** - **2.8169** at n = 180, **2.8504** at n = 58, **2.8523** at n = 56, **2.8821** at n = 36 - from an independently implemented inverse incomplete beta function whose t-quantiles are verified against table values to four decimals at df = 9, 35 and 57. One figure is measured **better** than the fifty-first cycle measured it: the legacy leg's one-interval settlement offset is confirmed on **4,079** compared instants per instrument with **0** mismatches, against the fifty-first cycle's **93 of 93**.

(ii) **A fifth unstated convention is found, and it is the slow clock's left edge.** The window contains **192** Monday 00:00 UTC sample points (2022-01-03 through 2025-09-01 inclusive; 1337 days = 191 intervals, so 192 points), and the fifty-first cycle's **191** weekly samples is one fewer. The difference is a rule the text does not state: the first sample, 2022-01-03, has a seven-day trailing window (2021-12-27 to 2022-01-02) that the window's start truncates, because the series is truncated at 2022-01-01 00:00. The convention is now stated and is binding: **a weekly sample is retained only if all seven of its trailing calendar days carry a matched settlement; a sample whose trailing window is truncated by the window start is dropped, not averaged over the days that remain.** Under the alternative rule - averaging over the days that remain - the counts are **192** weekly samples, **61**/**65** extreme weeks and **37**/**37** independent 20-day windows, so the convention is worth one extreme week and one window per instrument, and the fifty-first cycle's recorded **191 / 60 / 64 / 36** figures are right under the rule now written down rather than under the text as it stood. The recorded **192** is a count of **Mondays**, not a count of **samples**, and the two are not interchangeable.

(iii) **The legacy product's row structure is corrected in place, and the correction moves the window's end by one settlement.** The v1.12 clause (i)'s sentence - "the legacy product's file for date D carries the three settlements of **D** at 00:00, 08:00 and 16:00" - is **superseded in place**. The file for date D carries three rows **labelled** D 00:00, D 08:00 and D 16:00, but the `real_funding_rate` in each row is the rate that **settled** at the row's label **minus 8 hours**, so the file for date D carries the three settlements **(D-1) 16:00, D 00:00 and D 08:00** - and never the D 16:00 settlement, which appears in file D+1. This is measured directly against the all-swap product on 2022-09-07, 2024-08-05 and 2025-09-07 with **0** mismatches, and the 4,079-instant cross-vintage comparison is consistent with it throughout. Two consequences follow. (a) **The legacy product's last settlement is 2025-09-07 08:00 UTC, not 2025-09-07 16:00**, so the thirty-second cycle's recorded "the last file is 2025-09-07 - three 8-hour settlements, the last at 2025-09-07 16:00 UTC" is **superseded in place**. (b) **The window's end is therefore one settlement beyond the legacy product's coverage, not exactly at it**: the recorded window's last matched settlement is 2025-09-07 16:00, which the legacy product cannot supply. The window's end is accordingly declared as what it is - **a declared pull boundary, chosen at 2025-09-08 00:00 UTC exclusive, and not a pre-registered date and not a data-imposed limit** - and the reason the fifty-first cycle gave for it is corrected in the same breath. A second, **silent** hazard sits in the same product and is now recorded: **the legacy files for 2021 carry no header row at all** (the first row of each file is data, and the `contract_type` field reads `SWAP` rather than the bilingual header the 2022-and-later files carry). A reader who parses those files with a header assumption silently discards one data row per file and computes **731** pre-window matched settlements instead of **1,096** - a 33% error, with no error message, arising entirely from a file-format change inside the same archive.

(iv) **The legacy vintage's whole count set is measured, and the count set is vintage-stable.** The untouched pre-backfill product alone - the legacy per-instrument daily files, **2,692** per instrument over 2021-01-01 to 2025-09-07, with **no** all-swap file anywhere - was used as the second venue's leg for the entire window. It reproduces **4,036** matched settlements (one fewer than the canonical **4,037**, because the legacy product's last settlement is 2025-09-07 08:00), **3,766** eligible, and then **to the digit on every other count**: **738** trigger settlements for BTC (**348** upper, **390** lower) and **734** for ETH (**338** upper, **396** lower), **310** and **303** merged episodes, **180** independent 5-day windows for both instruments, **58** and **56** independent 20-day windows, and the slow clock's **191** weekly samples, **60**/**64** extreme weeks and **36**/**36** independent 20-day windows. The cross-vintage value comparison over **4,079** common settlements per instrument finds **0** differing values, so the rolling backfill re-published **1,356** files without altering a single funding rate. **The recorded count set is therefore vintage-invariant, and the only sensitivity the backfill introduced was the addition of one settlement at the right edge of the window.** The plan now says so, and a validator is told that the legacy product may be used for the whole window rather than only for the 48 settlements the all-swap product does not carry.

(v) **The net-of-carry accrual rule is made executable, and the literature's carry figure is explicitly not the carry on this pair.** The v1.12 clause (vii) requires the registered statistic to be reported net of the funding differential accrued over the forward window but does not say how to compute it, so the rule is now written out. Let the forward window run from the trigger settlement **t0** to **t1** on the common 8-hour grid; let **d_s** be the pair difference at settlement **s** (the publisher's funding rate minus the second venue's funding rate at the same grid point, each as a per-settlement rate on the 8-hour interval); then the accrued differential over the window is **A = prod over s in (t0, t1] of (1 + 8 * d_s) - 1**, with the simple sum **8 * sum over s of d_s** reported alongside it, the set of settlements included being exactly the grid points in the half-open interval, and the sign convention declared: **a positive d means the publisher's venue is the expensive one, so a long-the-cheap / short-the-expensive position accrues +A**. The registered statistic is the venue-relative price-return difference **minus** A, and the gross figure is reported beside it. Two qualifications are recorded. (a) **The ~7% annualised figure the plan cites is not this pair's carry**: the source (Lau, SSRN 6993978, read at Crossref on 2026-10-21) reports a cross-venue spread of roughly 7% annualised between **Hyperliquid and the centralised venues**, and separately reports a *single-venue* premium of only about **2-3%** on Binance and Bybit; the entry's pair is **centralised against centralised**, so the relevant carry is the *difference* of two single-venue premia and may be near zero, small or negative - the netting must use the pair's own measured accrued differential, never the literature's headline number. (b) **The accrual is a funding quantity, not a return quantity**, so computing it stays inside this repository's scope; what stays outside it is the price-return difference the netting is applied to.

(vi) **The block structure is completed, and the bootstrap's own parameters are declared.** The v1.12 clause (vi) declared the block (the registered forward window on the instantaneous construction, a moving block of at least four weekly observations on the slow clock) and the 2/4/8-block sensitivity. The remaining free parameters are now fixed: on the slow clock the block length **B** is stated in **weekly observations** (**B = 2, 4, 8** reported, with **B = 4** as the pre-registered primary), the number of blocks in a replicate is **ceil(n / B)**, blocks are drawn **with replacement** from the **eligible** weekly observations only, a block's start is a uniformly chosen eligible weekly observation, the block bootstrap is run for **10,000** replicates, **SE_block** is the standard deviation of the replicates of the registered statistic's mean, and the sensitivity of **SE_block** - not only of the MDE - to B is reported. On the instantaneous construction the windows are already non-overlapping by construction, so the block is the window itself and no bootstrap of blocks is required; the 5-day and 20-day window counts are the **n** that enter the multiplier, and the multiplier is quoted with **n** attached in every instance.

(vii) **The null clause is completed, and the threshold it is compared against is itself pre-registered.** The fifty-first cycle's clause made the null publishable only if **SE_block** and the resulting MDE are reported with it, and otherwise made the null *uninformative*. That is necessary and not sufficient, because an MDE that is not compared against a pre-registered economically meaningful difference does not license a null in either direction. The clause now reads: **the null may be reported as evidence of no effect only if (a) SE_block and the MDE are reported; (b) the MDE is compared against an economically meaningful difference, D*, that was pre-registered before the window opened, and the null is reported as evidence of no effect only when MDE < D*; and (c) the block structure, the window counts and the eligible denominator are quoted with the result.** If no D* was pre-registered before the window opened, the null is reported as **uninformative** with the window counts stated, and the MDE is reported as the smallest effect the sample could have detected. **D* is not supplied by this cycle**, because supplying it after the window has opened would be exactly the post-hoc choice the clause forbids, and the entry's own cost model does not fix one; this is a named open input for the validator, not an omission.

(viii) **None of this changes the registered prediction.** The sign of the venue-relative mapping remains untested and is not guessed; the registered measurement, the horizons, the comparator and the null's *conclusion* are unchanged. The amendments make the measurement reproducible by a third party - which this cycle has now demonstrated on a second pull with a second implementation - they fix a fifth unstated convention, they correct the legacy product's row structure in place, they make the net-of-carry rule computable, and they complete the block structure and the null clause. **No dimension moves and the total stays at 55** (12+3+6+15+3+8+8), for the reason recorded in item 16.
**Amended in v1.14 (fifty-third cycle - the window's end is declared and the cost of the declaration is recorded, the threshold the null clause is compared against is given a derivation rule that does not require the outcome, and both legs' availability boundaries are re-verified by a fresh pull; written before any outcome measurement, and no outcome has been measured for this entry at any point in this catalogue).** (i) **The window is declared: [2022-01-01 00:00 UTC, 2026-09-30 16:00 UTC] on the 8-hour settlement grid.** The window's start is unchanged. Its end is the publisher's funding archive's last settlement, so the window is now a **data-availability boundary and not a pull artefact**, and the rule that fixes it is: *the window ends at the last settlement instant for which both legs are available, and the end is recorded in the registration document before the first outcome is measured.* The fifty-first cycle's recorded end, 2025-09-08 00:00 UTC exclusive, is **superseded in place** because it was a boundary produced by the second venue's **legacy** per-instrument product stopping on 2025-09-07 - a discontinuation artefact with no economic meaning - while the second venue's **all-swap** product, which carries the same data and has been published since 2022-01-17, runs to **2026-10-20**; re-verified on 2026-10-21, the all-swap file for 2026-10-20 answers **HTTP 200** and the file for 2026-10-21 answers **HTTP 404** (next-day publication), while the legacy per-instrument file for 2025-09-07 answers **HTTP 200** and those for 2025-09-08, 2025-10-01 and 2025-12-01 all answer **HTTP 404**. The declared window's count set is the extended one already on the record and re-verified this cycle: **5,201** matched settlements, **4,931** eligible, **997/993** trigger settlements, **413/408** episodes, **238/243** and **76/74** independent windows, against the short window's **4,037**, **3,767**, **738/734**, **310/303**, **180/180** and **58/56**. The short window's counts stay on the record as the conservative reading and every power claim must be quoted with the window stated.

(ii) **The cost of the declaration is recorded.** The extension adds **1,164** matched settlements, about **+29%** on the binding number, and adds **12.9 months** of data that the original window did not contain; that additional period is not free of regime risk - it spans a period in which both venues' contract populations changed - and a validator who reports only the extended window's counts is reporting the more powerful test and must say so. The declaration was made **before** any outcome was measured, and it was made on a data-availability rule and not on the counts; the counts are quoted above as a consequence, and the plan now requires the window's counts and the MDE's window to be stated together so that a reader can always recover which sample a power claim belongs to.

(iii) **The threshold the null clause is compared against is given a derivation rule, so the null clause is executable without the outcome.** The v1.13 clause (vii) requires the minimum detectable effect to be compared against an economically meaningful difference **D\*** pre-registered before the window opened, and no D\* exists; supplying a number now would be the post-hoc choice the clause forbids, so this cycle writes the **rule** that makes D\* computable without reference to the result. **D\* is set as a fixed multiple of the round-trip trading cost on the registered statistic's own units, taken from the two venues' published taker-fee schedules as they stand on the registration date, expressed net of the funding differential accrued over the forward window** (the v1.13 clause (v) requirement, which is why the accrual enters the threshold and not only the statistic), with the multiple fixed in the plan at **three** and not tunable to the result; the fee schedules are free, dated and access 1, so the rule is executable by a third party; and **a validator who cannot state a D\* in the registration document may not publish a null**, which is the force the clause needs. The catalogue does not supply a D\* number, because supplying one now would be the act the clause forbids, and because the fee schedules are the validator's to read on their own registration date.

(iv) **Both legs' availability and the publisher's settlement structure are re-verified by a fresh pull today.** The publisher's monthly per-symbol `fundingRate` archive was pulled again for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT: **162** files, **7,395** settlements per symbol, 2020-01-01 00:00 to 2026-09-30 16:00 with at most **2 ms** of jitter, **every** row's `funding_interval_hours` equal to **8** read from the file's own column, **no** duplicate `calc_time` and **no** two settlements in one 8-hour grid bucket. Inside the declared window the publisher's leg has **5,202** grid instants, against the record's **5,201** matched, so exactly one publisher instant in the window is unmatched by the second venue; **2,193** settlements precede the window. The vintage-stability finding of the fifty-second cycle - the count set is reproducible on the untouched legacy product alone - is unaffected and is not re-run this cycle.

(v) **None of this changes the registered prediction.** The sign of the venue-relative mapping remains untested, the third-venue question remains open, and the entry's effective sample is a function of the declared window, which is now declared rather than inherited. No dimension moves.

**Amended in v1.15 (fifty-third cycle, completion and verification pass - the binding count is re-derived on a fresh pull of both legs by an independent implementation, the timestamp-matching rule the plan never stated is written down, and the window's end is found to rest on a rule that is not idempotent; written after the verification was executed and before any outcome measurement, and no outcome has been measured for this entry at any point in this catalogue).** (i) **The binding count is re-derived, and the plan's matching rule is found to be unstated and load-bearing.** On a fresh pull of both legs - the publisher's monthly per-symbol `fundingRate` archive for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT (**162** files, **7,395** settlements per symbol, 2020-01-01 00:00 to 2026-09-30 16:00, every row's `funding_interval_hours` equal to **8** read from the file's own column, no duplicate `calc_time`, every settlement on the 8-hour grid with a single-valued spacing histogram of **8.000 hours** over all 7,394 intervals, **5,202** grid instants inside the declared window and **2,193** before it) and the second venue's **all-swap** daily product swept day by day from 2022-01-01 to 2026-10-02 (**1,736** files, of which the first **16** do not exist because the product begins on 2022-01-17) together with the **legacy** per-instrument product - the number of publisher instants inside the declared window that the second venue covers is **tolerance-dependent**: **5,152** for BTC and **4,844** for ETH under exact timestamp equality, **5,153** and **5,172** at plus or minus one second, **5,200** and **5,199** at plus or minus five and sixty seconds, and **5,200** for both at plus or minus two minutes. The recorded **5,201** is reproduced **only** by a third reading - a **floor-to-grid bucket join**, in which a second-venue timestamp is attached to the grid instant it falls inside - and that reading is not innocuous: on 2022-12-18 the second venue recorded an **off-grid settlement at 18:54:00**, two hours and fifty-four minutes past the 16:00 grid point, carrying the **same rate in both of its own products** (BTC −0.000012515715975, ETH 0.0000367080042939), and the regular 16:00 settlement is **absent from both products**; the bucket join silently attaches that settlement to 16:00, while a tolerance join correctly leaves 2022-12-18 16:00 unmatched. The plan therefore states the rule: **the two legs are matched on the publisher's 8-hour grid; a second-venue settlement is matched to a grid instant only if it falls inside that instant's half-open 8-hour bucket; a settlement that falls in no bucket, and two settlements in one bucket, are both reported as anomalies and the grid instant is reported as unmatched.** Under that rule the second venue's coverage inside the declared window is **5,200 of 5,202** for both instruments, and the one publisher instant unmatched by **both** second-venue products is **2022-02-25 08:00** - the legacy file for 2022-02-25 carries two rows and the all-swap file for the same date carries two, so the settlement never entered either record. The recorded **5,201** is therefore retained as the bucket-join reading and is **superseded in place** by **5,200** as the plan's count under the stated rule; the one-instant difference is located, named and explained rather than left as an unexplained gap, and the derived counts (4,931 eligible, 997/993 trigger settlements, 413/408 episodes, 238/243 and 76/74 independent windows) were measured on the larger reading and are therefore **upper bounds by one settlement**, with the direction of the effect unknown, because the unmatched instant is an ordinary in-window settlement that could fall in either arm. (ii) **The window's end is a rule that is not idempotent, and the rule is replaced by a registration.** The v1.14 clause fixed the window's end by the rule "the window ends at the last settlement instant for which both legs are available". Measured today, the second venue's all-swap product answers **HTTP 200** for the file of **2026-10-21** - the same file that answered **404** earlier on the same day when the fifty-third cycle probed it - and **404** for 2026-10-22, so that boundary moves intraday; and the publisher has **no daily funding-rate product at all** (HTTP **404** for 2024-05-05 and 2024-05-06 as well as for 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21), so its leg is bound to the **monthly** product, whose last file is 2026-09. The declared window's end, **2026-09-30 16:00**, is confirmed as the publisher's last settlement, but the *rule* that fixes it will silently extend the window the moment the publisher publishes its 2026-10 monthly file, and every count, every minimum detectable effect and every power claim attached to the window would then change without a decision being taken. The clause is replaced: **the window is a registration and not a rule - it is [2022-01-01 00:00 UTC, 2026-09-30 16:00 UTC] on the 8-hour settlement grid, fixed at the moment of declaration, with the availability evidence recorded at that moment (the publisher's last monthly file 2026-09; the second venue's last all-swap file 2026-10-21); any extension is a new registration with a new version stamp and the cost of the extension recorded; and a validator who re-runs the plan on later data must quote the window it used.** (iii) **The publisher's leg's jitter is corrected in place.** The fifty-third cycle's source note records the publisher's settlements as carrying "at most **2 ms** of jitter"; measured across all 7,395 settlements per symbol the maximum deviation from the 8-hour grid is **47 ms** (4,083 settlements exactly on the grid, 793 at +1 ms, 297 at +2 ms, 249 at +5 ms, the remainder smaller), which is the figure the fifty-first cycle had already recorded. The correction changes no count - the grid position is unaffected - but it is one of the two reasons the leg's timestamps cannot be compared by equality, and therefore one of the reasons the matching rule had to be written. The second leg carries its own jitter: **310** of the ETH leg's rows carry 1 to 3 ms of it, one row carries **+61 s**, the BTC leg carries one row at +1 ms and one at the +2 h 54 min anomaly of 2022-12-18. (iv) **None of this changes the registered prediction.** The sign of the venue-relative mapping remains untested and is not guessed; the registered measurement, the horizons, the comparator and the null's conclusion are unchanged. The amendments make the measurement reproducible by a third party on a stated window under a stated matching rule. **No dimension moves and the total stays at 55** (12+3+6+15+3+8+8), for the reason recorded in item 16.

**Amended in v1.16 (fifty-sixth cycle - the window extension is priced to the instant, the declared window is kept as the binding reading, and the extension is registered as a declared option with a fixed ceiling; written after the pricing was executed and before any outcome measurement).** (i) **The declared window's size is re-derived independently, and the cost of the next extension is measured to the instant.** The declared window **[2022-01-01 00:00 UTC, 2026-09-30 16:00 UTC]** on the 8-hour grid contains **5,202** instants, re-derived on 2026-10-22 by enumerating the grid itself and matching the recorded publisher-instant count exactly. The publisher's **next** monthly file (2026-10) would carry the window forward to 2026-10-31 16:00, i.e. **93** additional grid instants, or **1.79%** of the declared window - and that is now the **ceiling**, because the publisher's next monthly file is the last file that could ever be absorbed. The second venue's all-swap product has **advanced by one day** since the fifty-fourth cycle recorded it answering **404** for 2026-10-21: that file now answers **HTTP 200**, so **63** of the 93 extension instants (**1.21%** of the declared window) are covered by the second venue's leg today, and every one of the 21 October files carries exactly **9 settlements for the three instruments** - **3 each** for BTC-USDT-SWAP, ETH-USDT-SWAP and BTC-USD-SWAP - with no interior gap over the extension period. The observation is dated to the minute, because the boundary moved **intraday on the same calendar date** the fifty-fourth cycle recorded it as absent: re-probed at **2026-10-22 02:04 UTC**, the 2026-10-21 file answers **200** and the 2026-10-22 file answers **404**. The publisher's leg contributes **0**: its 2026-10 monthly file is not published (81 monthly zips for BTCUSDT, the last being 2026-09) and the publisher has **no daily funding-rate product at all** (HTTP 404 for 2026-10-20, 2026-10-21 and 2024-05-05).

(ii) **Decision: the declared window is kept as the binding reading, and the extension is recorded as a priced, declared option rather than taken.** The reasons are recorded here so that a later cycle inherits the decision rather than re-deriving it. (a) **The extension is immaterial to every count the entry depends on**: at most **93** grid instants on a window of **5,202**, i.e. **1.79%**, and the binding counts (eligible settlements, trigger settlements, episodes, independent windows) are bounded above by that fraction, which cannot change a sign, a threshold comparison or a minimum detectable effect of the order the entry declares. (b) **The extension is not currently constructible**: the publisher's leg is **0 of 93**, so registering the extension today would register a window whose data leg does not exist, and a registration is supposed to be executable. (c) **A registered window that re-evaluates is a rule and not a registration** - the fifty-third cycle's finding - so any extension is necessarily a *new* registration with a new version stamp, and a new registration for a 1.79% sample increase is a cost the entry should not pay before its first result exists. (d) **The extension's cost is now fixed rather than moving**, because the ceiling is the publisher's next monthly file; the option can therefore be priced once and taken later under a declared rule, which is what the fifty-fourth cycle asked for when it recorded the extension as a cost rather than a result.

(iii) **The rule under which the option may be taken is written down now, so that taking it later is a decision and not a drift.** If a later cycle takes the extension, it must (i) be a **new registration** with its own version stamp, (ii) be labelled a **confirmatory** extension, (iii) be executed only after the publisher's 2026-10 monthly file is published, so that the two legs are both complete over the extension period, (iv) be executed **only before any outcome in the extended period has been read** - the extension is not a route to a favourable sample - and (v) carry the cost recorded here: **93 grid instants, 1.79% of the declared window, of which 63 were covered by the second venue and 0 by the publisher on 2026-10-22**.

(iv) **The fifty-fourth cycle's recorded extension cost is retained, and it is a different quantity, so both are kept and labelled.** The recorded **+1,164 matched settlements (about +29% on 4,931 eligible) and 12.9 months of additional data** is the cost of the **declaration** - the move from the fifty-first cycle's pull boundary of 2025-09-08 to the declared end of 2026-09-30 16:00 - and it remains the cost of the declaration. The cost of the **next** extension, priced here, is **93 grid instants**, roughly **+1.8%** on the window and correspondingly on the eligible count, and it is *not* the same number and must not be quoted as one. Recording them together under one label would overstate the second by an order of magnitude, which is the failure mode this catalogue's audit rules exist to catch.
**Amended in v1.17 (fifty-seventh cycle - the entry's construction counts are re-derived on the declared window from the plan's own text on a fresh pull of both legs, the plan's matching-rule text and the plan's own matching count are found to disagree by one settlement, the disagreement is shown to move no derived count at all, the block bootstrap's design parameters and the minimum detectable effect are re-derived as a function of the realised independent-window count, and the extension's condition is re-tested and found unmet; written before any outcome measurement).**
(i) **The declared window's counts re-derive exactly from the plan's text, on a fresh pull of both legs.** The publisher's leg was re-pulled from the archive's monthly funding-rate product (81 monthly files per instrument, 2020-01 to 2026-09, **7,395** settlements per instrument) and the second venue's leg from its all-swap daily product (2022-01-17 to 2026-10-21, **10,432** settlement rows per instrument) with its legacy per-instrument product covering 2022-01-01 to 2022-01-16 (**96** rows). The window's **5,202** eight-hour grid instants re-derive, the publisher's maximum timestamp jitter re-derives at **47 ms**, the second venue's **310** ETH rows carrying 1-3 ms of jitter and its single **+61 s** row re-derive, the genuinely absent settlement at **2022-02-25 08:00** re-derives, and the off-grid **2022-12-18 18:54:00** settlement re-derives with the **same rate in both products** (**-0.000012515715975** for BTC, **-0.000011750308600** for ETH). On the bucket-join reading the counts are **5,201** matched, **4,931** eligible, **997**/**993** trigger settlements with the same tail splits (**488**/**509** for BTC and **475**/**518** for ETH), **413**/**408** episodes, **238**/**243** independent windows at 5 days and **76**/**74** at 20 days, and on the slow clock **247** weekly samples, **235** eligible, **77**/**90** extreme weeks and **46**/**49** independent 20-day windows. The fifty-third cycle's short-window figures reproduce exactly under the same implementation (**4,037** matched, **191** weekly samples, **60**/**64** extreme weeks, **36**/**36** independent 20-day windows), which is the check that the implementation is the entry's own and not a new one.
(ii) **The plan's matching-rule text and the plan's own matching count disagree by one settlement, and the disagreement moves no derived count.** The rule as written - "a second-venue settlement is matched to a grid instant only if it falls inside that instant's half-open 8-hour bucket" - attaches the off-grid 18:54 settlement to 2022-12-18 16:00 and gives **5,201**; the plan's recorded count of **5,200** is what the **tolerance** reading (+/- 120 s) gives, which leaves 2022-12-18 16:00 unmatched and reports two unmatched instants against the plan's "the one publisher instant unmatched by both second-venue products". **A third party re-deriving the plan's rule as written therefore gets 5,201 and not the recorded 5,200**, which is the fourth specification defect this entry has carried. The defect is now measured rather than argued, and the measurement is what makes it immaterial: **the two readings produce identical derived counts.** Under both, the trigger settlements are **997**/**993** with the same tail splits, the episodes are **413**/**408**, the independent windows are **238**/**243** at 5 days and **76**/**74** at 20 days, and the slow clock's counts are identical; only the matched count (5,201 against 5,200) and the eligible count (4,931 against 4,930) move, by one. **The fifty-fourth cycle's caveat that the binding numbers are "upper bounds by one settlement" can therefore be closed: the derived numbers are the same under either reading, so they are not bounds, they are the numbers.** The rule text is nevertheless amended in place to state the tolerance reading explicitly, so that the count and the text agree.
(iii) **The block bootstrap's design parameters and the minimum detectable effect are re-derived as a function of the realised independent-window count.** The design is unchanged - a block bootstrap with the cross-section kept intact within blocks, median-based summaries, no Sharpe ratio, alpha 0.05 two-sided, power 0.80, and the multiplier **t(1-alpha/2, n-1) + t(power, n-1)** applied to the block standard error, with the instantaneous clock's block equal to the forward window (5 or 20 days) and the slow clock's block a moving block of at least four weekly observations (28 days) with a 2/4/8-weekly sensitivity. The multiplier is re-derived from an independently implemented inverse incomplete beta function whose t-quantiles verify against table values to four decimals at df = 9, 35 and 57, and it reproduces the four recorded values to the digit: **2.8169** at n = 180, **2.8504** at n = 58, **2.8523** at n = 56 and **2.8821** at n = 36. On the declared window's realised counts the multipliers are **2.8132** (n = 238), **2.8129** (n = 243), **2.8385** (n = 76), **2.8396** (n = 74), **2.8638** (n = 46) and **2.8598** (n = 49) - the last two on the slow clock, where the declared window's realised independent-window count is **46** and **49** against the short window's 36. **The slow clock's effective sample has therefore grown by 28% and 36% over the declared window, and the MDE falls with it**: the plan's four recorded multipliers are the short window's and must be re-quoted against the declared window's counts before any power statement is made on the extended window.
(iv) **The extension's condition is re-tested and is not met.** Checked on 2026-10-22: the publisher's next monthly funding file, `data/futures/um/monthly/fundingRate/{SYMBOL}/{SYMBOL}-fundingRate-2026-10.zip`, answers **HTTP 404** - it is not published, and the publisher has no daily funding-rate product - while the second venue's all-swap daily product's last available file is **2026-10-21**, with 2026-10-22 answering **HTTP 404**. **The extension's condition is therefore still unmet on the publisher's leg, exactly as the fifty-sixth cycle recorded, and the declared window stands as the binding reading.** The extension's priced ceiling is unchanged at **93** grid instants (1.79% of the window) and remains a declared option under the v1.16 rule; nothing here takes it.
(v) The v1.3 specification items, the v1.4 to v1.14 clauses and the v1.15 and v1.16 clauses are otherwise unchanged, and none of these counts is a return statistic. **No dimension moves and the total stays at 55**, for the reason recorded in item 16.

(vi) **None of this changes the registered prediction** (this is the v1.16 amendment's closing clause; the v1.17 amendment was inserted above it and the label collision is repaired in place so that the two amendments' clause numbers do not collide). The sign of the venue-relative mapping remains untested and is not guessed; the null clause, the minimum detectable effect and the block structure are untouched; and the entry's two-venue construction, its matching rule and its declared window are unchanged. **No dimension moves and the total stays at 55** (12+3+6+15+3+8+8), for the reason recorded in item 16.

(vii) **Two figures in this amendment are corrected in place, one a mis-count and one a mis-transcription, and both are re-verified live.** (a) The second venue's all-swap leg carries **5,216 settlement rows per instrument** - **10,432** across the two instruments - not the 10,432 *per instrument* this amendment first stated. The leg's first available file is the one for **2022-01-17**, which carries the settlement instant **2022-01-16 16:00 UTC**, and its last is the file for **2026-10-21**, which carries the last settlement instant **2026-10-21 08:00 UTC**, over **1,740** distinct days with at most three settlements a day and a minimum of one. The mis-count moves no derived number, because every derived count is computed on the **matched** instants and not on the row count - the trigger settlements, episodes and independent windows are identical under both readings - but a row count is a reported quantity and is corrected rather than left. (b) The off-grid settlement's **ETH** rate is **+0.0000367080042939**; the **BTC** rate **-0.000012515715975** is confirmed. Both are re-verified on 2026-10-22 against the second venue's **two** products directly: the all-swap daily file for **2022-12-18** carries the row at **2022-12-18 18:54:00 UTC**, and the legacy per-instrument file for **2022-12-19** carries a row whose `funding_time` is **2022-12-19 02:54:00 UTC** and whose `real_funding_rate` is the same number - the same one-period settlement offset the fifty-first cycle confirmed on 93 of 93 compared instants, here applied to the off-grid instant itself. The off-grid instant is therefore confirmed to be present in both products with an identical rate, which is the catalogue's point, but the ETH value carried by the earlier text was transcribed wrongly and the wrong number is replaced in place rather than deleted. The wrong figure is also the only place in the record where a sign error survived a verification: the confirmation that "the same rate in both products" holds is independent of which of the two rates it is, so the equality was established while the value was wrong.

(verdict 2026-08-28; access 1 for the document): on a common window 2018-08-17 to 2026-07-05 the deployed momentum-rotation book reproduces to the published digits (K = 2: CAGR +42.91%, Sharpe 1.47, MDD -29.01%) and widening the selection degrades it (K = 3 Sharpe 1.61, K = 5 1.40, K = 8 1.27, with drawdown worse at every breadth above 2); the document's mechanistic reading is that H66's carry result does not transfer to momentum rotation, because carry harvests a premium paid by roughly 20 near-independent funding streams while rotation *selects*, so diluting a selection edge with weaker picks lowers the mean faster than it lowers the variance, and it explicitly records the select-versus-harvest distinction as "a hypothesis, not a rule" because it is one measurement in each of two families. martex-quant ledger H72 "Point-in-Time Carry" (verdict 2026-08-28; access 1 for the document), whose full text was read in the tenth cycle beyond the summary already on file: the hypothesis *predicted* that carry would survive an honest point-in-time universe where momentum would not, and it did - 86% of Sharpe retained (5.61 to 4.83) against momentum's 58% (1.47 to 0.86), with CAGR halving (+4.36% to +2.35%), a better drawdown (-0.78% to -0.35%), and a stated mechanism (rotation selects and is handed winners by a hindsight list; carry harvests and a biased list changes which streams are averaged and little else); the overlap between the point-in-time top-40 and the hindsight universe is 28-32% in the key years and rises to 52% by 2025, i.e. the universes are equally contaminated and the edges are not equally damaged; the document also states the caveat this entry inherits - contracts delisted after a collapse are absent from the pool, so the *sign* of the delisting bias on a book that is short the perp through exactly those events is genuinely unknown - and that carry earns approximately zero in 2025-2026 in every arm, the fifth independent confirmation of that finding after H62, H63 and H65. **The tenth cycle's finding: none of these three results tests CRYPTO-EDGE-003's registered mapping.** They test the *construction family* into which the entry's cost arithmetic has pushed it, and they say three things that bear directly on the entry: a selection rule is the weaker form of this trade; the harvest alternative is the form that is robust to universe bias and that earns approximately nothing today; and the harvest form's distinctive content over a selection form is documented to be nil in the strongest available evidence. Original source list continues: He, Manela, Ross & Wachter (2026), "Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures", arXiv:2212.06888 (v7, 17 Sep 2026), confirmed free - funding rates tend to be similar across exchanges because of cross-exchange arbitrage but can diverge in extreme liquidity episodes; the residual dispersion is attributed to segmented arbitrage (no cross-margining, each leg separately funded and margined) and to liquidity differences across exchanges; Binance-Bybit funding correlation of 0.74 with meaningful divergences during large funding payments; the authors state that residual cross-exchange dispersion reflects limits to arbitrage across segmented venues and is a promising avenue for future research (mechanism evidence and prior-art scoping).
