Net value after frictions 1/5 is held, and is now *evidenced* rather than merely inferred, since a peer-reviewed source finds many cross-sectional momentum portfolios are liquidated and those with significant mean returns often earn negative profits, and an independent 15-minute study puts the gross edge at 1.3 basis points per trade against a 5 basis-point round trip. **Fourteenth cycle: no dimension moves; the total is 45, re-derived as 12+6+3+9+3+8+4.** The cycle's evidence about this entry is **about its base, not about its registered state-dependence claim**, and the entry's three floors (robustness 1/5, net value after frictions 1/5, and the entry's confidence) are already at the bottom of their scales for reasons documented in v1.3 and v1.4, so nothing can fall; and no source in the cycle supports the registered claim, so nothing can rise. What the cycle changed is the **status of the size-composition confound, which the thirteenth cycle recorded as hypothetical and which is now documented three times over.** The size-momentum source is located and dated (SSRN 6628860, a working-paper preprint) and is corroborated by two stronger sources — a NBER working paper that finds small coins have systematically lower forward returns (the size factor, long the smallest and short the largest, earns +3.4% weekly) and a working paper that finds reversals are more pronounced in smaller and less liquid coins. The consequence is sharp and it is the reason no dimension moves rather than the reason one does: **the free screen and the published screen do not merely select differently sized populations, they can select populations whose base momentum spread has the opposite sign**, so a free replication's null is uninterpretable unless the base spread is estimated on the same population first and the comparison is made within a size stratum. That is now a **specification requirement** (item 14, v1.6) and a **null-outcome clarification**, not a score movement, because the dimension that would have to move is free-data accessibility and the entry's free replication remains *possible* — it is only uninterpretable if run without the two new requirements, and the cycle has specified it so that it is interpretable. **A recorded disagreement, restated and strengthened:** a reader could argue free-data accessibility 3/5 → 2/5 (total **43**, -2) on the ground that the free screen does not merely approximate the published screen but can select a population with a *different sign of the base effect*, so a free replication cannot test the entry's claim without the paid-tier screen, and the entry's published construction has already been documented to depend on that paid tier. The cycle still declines the move, and the reason is unchanged and now stronger: the free-data dimension asks whether the *essential input* of the claim — a point-in-time cross-sectional universe with a dispersion state and a momentum ranking — is constructible on free, dated data, and it is; the size-composition problem is a **confound within** the free construction, and the cycle's response to it is to specify the two requirements that make the free replication interpretable (declare the size composition, and estimate the base spread on the same population with a size-matched control), not to declare the input unobtainable. The alternative placement is recorded rather than dismissed. Rank 3, unchanged, and 7 points behind CRYPTO-EDGE-003.

**Amended in v1.7 (fifteenth cycle — the binding input is no longer unobtainable: a free, dated, point-in-time market-capitalisation panel exists, and the catalogue's recorded "unobtainable" determination is superseded in place).** (i) **The free point-in-time size proxy the thirteenth and fourteenth cycles said did not exist, does exist.** The Coin Metrics v4 **community** API (`https://community-api.coinmetrics.io/v4/timeseries/asset-metrics?assets=btc&metrics=CapMrktCurUSD`, access 1, keyless, HTTP 200, verified 2026-10-20) returns a **daily, dated, point-in-time market-capitalisation series** (`CapMrktCurUSD`) with history to genesis for the majors — BTC from 2010-08-24, ETH from 2015-11-06, LTC from 2013-05-20, DOGE from 2014-03-16, XRP from 2014-10-02, ADA from 2018-01-14, BNB from 2017-08-30 — and the asset catalogue shows **135 assets carrying a community-tier market-cap metric** against a full catalogue of 6,347 assets. This **supersedes in place** the catalogue's recorded determination that "historical market capitalisation and market-cap rank remain unavailable on every free tier the catalogue has checked (CoinGecko, CoinPaprika, CoinLore, CoinMarketCap, DefiLlama)", which is no longer true and must not be repeated. The routes tested and found empty in the same cycle remain empty and are recorded in SOURCE_NOTES.md: CoinGecko's free tier refuses historical queries (HTTP 429 on `days=90` and `days=365`), CoinPaprika's historical endpoint returns HTTP 402, CoinLore's coin endpoint HTTP 403, CoinMarketCap's historical endpoint HTTP 500, DefiLlama has no per-token historical supply endpoint (HTTP 404 on all five forms tried), and Blockchair, Etherscan v2, Dune, Santiment, Messari, Kaiko, Blockscout, mempool.space and Signals Analytics are key-gated or current-only. (ii) **The free panel's composition remains the binding limitation, and it is a limitation of *coverage*, not of *access*.** The 135-asset community panel is survivor-only, listing-biased and large-cap-skewed, so the smallest size quintile in which the published base effect is documented (the -4.9% weekly reversal in the smallest quintile against +1.0% in the largest) **is not reachable from it**, and the free screen therefore still cannot reproduce the published screen's size composition. A turnover proxy built from the venue's own daily klines (about 1,000 spot symbols, `quote_volume`) is available and dated, but it is a **liquidity** proxy, confounded with the very liquidity/reversal effect the size stratum is meant to control for, and must be declared as a proxy if used. The entry's v1.6 specification — declare the free universe's size composition, estimate the unconditional momentum spread on the same population, and compare **within a size stratum** — therefore survives intact and is now executable with a market-cap-based stratum for 135 assets rather than only a proxy-based one. (iii) **The entry's registered prediction, its null outcome, its unconditional-spread control and its size-matched control are unchanged**, and no empirical validation was performed in this repository.

**Fifteenth cycle: no dimension moves; the total is 45, re-derived as 12+6+3+9+3+8+4.** The cycle's finding about this entry is a **free-data finding about a confound control**, and the standing rule applies: data access does not bear on a registered prediction. The entry's three floors (robustness 1/5, net value after frictions 1/5, confidence) are already at the bottom of their scales for reasons documented in v1.3 and v1.4, and no source in the cycle supports the registered state-dependence claim, so nothing can fall and nothing can rise. **The fourteenth cycle's recorded disagreement on free-data accessibility (3/5 -> 2/5, total 43) is now answered, and a new disagreement in the opposite direction is recorded and declined.** (a) The fourteenth cycle declined a downgrade to 2/5 on the ground that the size-composition problem is a **confound within** the free construction and that the cycle's response was to specify the two requirements that make the free replication interpretable, not to declare the input unobtainable. **This cycle vindicates that reasoning with a source**: the size proxy is *not* unobtainable — the Coin Metrics community tier supplies a free, dated, daily market-capitalisation panel for 135 assets — so the fourteenth cycle's refusal to treat the size-composition problem as an access failure was correct, and the recorded disagreement is marked **answered against the downgrade**. (b) **A new recorded disagreement, which the cycle declines: free-data accessibility 3/5 -> 4/5 (total 48).** A reader could argue that the entry's "binding input" is now constructible on free, dated data with a genuine market-capitalisation measure rather than a proxy, so the free-data score should rise one notch. The cycle declines the move and records the reason: the free panel reaches 135 large and mid-cap assets, so the free screen still cannot enter the smallest size quintile in which the published base effect has its documented sign; the dimension asks whether the *essential input of the registered claim* — a point-in-time cross-sectional universe carrying a dispersion state and a momentum ranking — is constructible, which it was already and which this cycle's finding improves without changing; and the size control is a **confound control**, with the entry's specification for it unchanged and still requiring the comparison to be made within a size stratum. **3/5 is held, the total stays at 45, and the alternative placement of 48 is recorded here rather than dismissed.** Rank 3, unchanged, and 7 points behind CRYPTO-EDGE-003.
**Seventeenth cycle: ONE dimension moves — free-data accessibility 3/5 -> 4/5 — and the total moves from 45 to 48, re-derived as 12+6+3+12+3+8+4. The ground the fifteenth cycle recorded for declining the upgrade is falsified by direct measurement, and the upgrade is made on the measurement's own terms.** The fifteenth cycle declined a recorded upgrade (3/5 -> 4/5, total 48) on one stated ground: "the free panel reaches 135 large and mid-cap assets, so the free screen still cannot enter the smallest size quintile in which the published base effect has its documented sign". **That ground is false, and this cycle measured it rather than re-arguing it.** The free point-in-time market-capitalisation panel is the Coin Metrics v4 community tier's `CapMrktCurUSD` series for 135 assets of a 6,347-asset catalogue (the fifteenth cycle's counts reproduced exactly), and at 2026-10-19 **104 panel assets carry a market cap**: minimum **$0.29m**, 5th percentile **$1.63m**, 25th percentile **$48.7m**, median **$239m**, maximum **$1,646.6bn**. The reference screen's own current size profile — CoinGecko's keyless top 500, 500 rows fetched live — is rank 100 **$630m**, rank 200 **$169m**, rank 300 **$91m**, rank 400 **$61m**, rank 500 **$46m**, so the published screen's bottom quintile is the **$46m-$61m** band today. **32 of the 104 panel assets are below $61m and 26 are below $46m**, and every one of the 32 has a series still current to 2026-10-19. The free screen therefore **does enter, and goes below, the smallest size quintile in which the published base effect has its documented sign**, and the fifteenth cycle's ground is **superseded in place**. *The replacement ground, dated, and available only because of the measurement that produced it:* the free screen's small stratum is **a different population** from the published screen's. Its small-cap tail is largely deprecated tokens (ZIL, ALPHA, POLY, KNC, SRM, DRGN, REN, XEM, PERP, GRIN, ICX, VET, OMG, BAL, LRC, CVC, GNT, SNT, UMA, POWR, ELF) plus four stablecoins (GUSD, BUSD, LUSD, USDC_TRX), and a cross-check against CoinGecko for 60 matched assets gives a median ratio of **0.992** with 90% within 3x but individual divergences of up to about **90x** in the small tail (VET: Coin Metrics $6.74m against CoinGecko $614.0m; USDD_ETH $123.97m against $1,766.39m). So the free screen's *ranking* inside the small stratum is not the published screen's ranking. **That is a specification matter, and it is handled as one, on exactly the reasoning the fourteenth cycle used when it declined a downgrade on the ground that a size-composition problem is a confound *within* the free construction and not an access failure.** The free-data dimension asks whether the **essential input of the registered claim** is constructible on free, dated data; it now is, with a **genuine market-capitalisation measure** rather than a proxy, and the size stratum is enterable, so the score moves to 4/5 — the level the catalogue's ladder assigns to "the essential inputs are free and dated, with a declared population restriction" — and the residual composition problem is discharged in the specification, not priced into the score. **Three specification clauses are added to item 14 in consequence.** (i) The free screen must **exclude stablecoins** and must apply a **liveness rule** — the asset must have traded on the date — so that the smallest stratum is not composed of defunct tokens; the panel's own catalogue shows several of its small-cap assets' series ending (one at 2023-03-03, another at 2024-11-07), which is exactly the contamination the rule must exclude. (ii) The free screen's **size composition must be reported per date against the reference screen's**, and the comparison must be made **within a size stratum** with the base spread estimated on the same population first — the v1.6 requirement, now executable with a market-cap-based stratum for a panel whose small end is live. (iii) The **market-cap values must be cross-checked against a second source at the stratum's boundary**, because the panel's small-cap values are not interchangeable with the reference screen's and a mis-ranked boundary asset would move the sign of the very spread the entry is about. **Every other dimension is unchanged, and the standing rule is applied unchanged.** The cycle's evidence is about *access and about the composition of a screen*, and bears on a registered prediction nowhere: the mechanism (3/5), evidence-quality (2/5), robustness (1/5), net-value (1/5), falsifiability (4/5) and originality (2/5) dimensions are all untouched; robustness and net value are at their floors for reasons documented in v1.1 to v1.4, and no source in the cycle supports the registered state-dependence claim, so nothing can fall and nothing can rise. **The entry's registered prediction, its null outcome, its unconditional-spread control and its size-matched control are unchanged, and no empirical validation was performed in this repository: no return, Sharpe ratio, drawdown, hit rate or win rate was computed for any strategy.** The total is 48, the entry remains rank 3 and **7 points behind CRYPTO-EDGE-003** and 10 behind CRYPTO-EDGE-001; the alternative placements of 43 (the fourteenth cycle's declined downgrade) and 48 are both recorded rather than dismissed. The honest summary is unchanged in substance and better founded in method: the entry is now testable on free data, it is still probably not worth much, and the free screen's small stratum is the one place where the published result and the free replication are most likely to disagree.
**Forty-eighth-cycle sources and measurements (2026-10-21).** (a) *The community tier's catalogue and the 84-asset common panel.* `https://community-api.coinmetrics.io/v4/catalog/assets` and `https://community-api.coinmetrics.io/v4/timeseries/asset-metrics?assets={LIST}&metrics=CapMrktCurUSD,CapMrktEstUSD&frequency=1d&start_time={D}&end_time={D}&page_size=10000`. Access 1, keyless. *Measured 2026-10-21:* the catalogue returns **6,347** assets with **135** carrying `CapMrktCurUSD` at 1d, **850** carrying `CapMrktEstUSD` and **901** distinct carrying one or the other, every figure reproducing the record; **84** carry both; the timeseries route still **requires an explicit `assets` parameter** and returns dated values for both metrics on one request. A per-asset pull of the **83** assets with a common window (**197,747 asset-days**) was executed. *Establishes:* the within-asset comparison the v1.9 clause required. *Does not establish:* any stratum composition statistic by itself, and no return statistic — the unconditional momentum spread and the within-stratum comparison remain return statistics and were not computed. (b) *The reference screen, re-fetched.* `https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/markets?vs_currency=usd&order=market_cap_desc&per_page=100&page=1..5`, access 1, keyless. *Measured 2026-10-21:* **500** rows, **494** distinct symbols, **500** distinct ids; the size profile and the **$60.3m** rank-400 bottom-quintile ceiling reproduce the record within 1-2%. *Establishes:* the ceiling used for the stratum-membership test. *Does not establish:* the screen's historical membership, which is current-only and remains the entry's binding limitation. (c) *The composition decomposition and the per-metric cross-check.* On the panel's final date: estimated **447** below the ceiling, current **32**, intersection **22**, **Jaccard 0.0481**; disjoint remainder **423** against **9**, intersection **0**, **Jaccard 0.000**; common panel **24** against **23**, intersection **22**, **Jaccard 0.88**. Boundary cross-check per metric: estimated **median 0.9936** (n = 277, 97.8% within [0.5, 2]), current **median 1.0021** (n = 44, 93.2% within [0.5, 2]), with the recorded outlier set reproduced exactly. *Establishes:* that the free screen's small stratum is a metric-determined population and that the composition gap is total wherever only one metric exists. *Does not establish:* any forward relationship, and no return, spread, drawdown, hit rate, win rate or Sharpe ratio was computed for any strategy.

**Forty-eighth cycle: no change, and the total stays at 48/100 with every dimension held (12+6+3+12+3+8+4), and the reason is recorded rather than assumed.** The cycle **executed** the within-asset metric comparison the forty-seventh cycle's clause required, and the finding is large and adverse to a clean replication: the two free market-cap definitions place an asset in **different strata on 4.77% of the common panel's asset-days** (9,428 of 197,747), affect **44 of the 83** assets with a common window at some point, and select **completely disjoint** small populations wherever only one definition is available (**423** against **9**, intersection **0**, Jaccard **0.000**) against the panel-wide **0.0481**. This is a **measurement fact about what the entry's input measures**; the entry's registered prediction concerns the *conditional* behaviour of the cross-sectional momentum spread in high- versus low-dispersion states, no return statistic was computed, and under the standing rule no dimension moves. **The dimension most exposed to a move was robustness (1/5), and the placement is declined with its reason stated.** The argument for moving it: a population that the pre-registered definition itself selects differently on one day in twenty, and whose two candidate definitions select *disjoint* small strata, is a robustness threat to any within-stratum comparison, because the comparison's population is not determined until the metric is chosen. The argument against, which the catalogue adopts: **the metric choice is a specification term that is now pre-registered in the plan of record and whose consequence is now measured and reported**, so the adversarial variation has been closed by a declaration and a measurement rather than left open; what remains open is the reference screen's *historical* membership, which is a supply-side limitation already recorded and is not a variation of the registered claim. Moving robustness on the metric-determination fact would move it on every future definitional clarification, and the rubric does not permit it. **A second placement is recorded rather than dismissed: free-data accessibility 4/5 -> 5/5, contribution 12 -> 15, total 48 -> 51**, on the ground that the community tier's panel is deep enough to carry the small stratum on a dated, point-in-time basis and the entry's essential input is confirmed free and dated at 1d across 901 assets; the decline is that the dimension prices the *accessibility* of the input, which was already determined at 4/5, while the cycle's finding is about **what the input measures** rather than about whether it can be obtained, and no accessibility change occurred. **The plan-of-record consequences are written into the plan of record:** the v1.9 cross-check pair (**0.97 / 0.98**) is superseded in place by the re-derived **0.9936 (n = 277)** and **1.0021 (n = 44)**, the cross-check must fix a sample rule before it is quoted again, and a new binding clause requires the **stratum's stability** — the count below the $60.3m ceiling, the entries and exits across it, and the turnover rate — to be reported under the pre-registered metric with stablecoin and deprecated-token membership declared per date. **The executed confirmation was written into the plan of record at CRYPTO-EDGE-004 item 14, v1.10**, superseding the v1.9 clause (iii) in place; the write is recorded here rather than assumed, and the carry-over free-data disagreement (4/5, total 48) was re-tested on its own terms and upheld. **Forty-ninth cycle amendment (2026-10-21) - no dimension moves; the total stays at 48, re-derived as 12+6+3+12+3+8+4.** The cycle executed the stratum-churn census the v1.10 clause required, on the 2,850-date registered panel window, with stablecoin and deprecated-token membership declared per date. The recorded exit decomposition **reproduces exactly at the $61m ceiling** (5,292 exits, 5,098 upward migrations, 194 panel deaths, 96.3% / 3.7%, median stratum 145, maximum 492, and all ten recorded stratum sizes to the digit), while the thirty-third cycle's own **5,323 / 5,286 / 225** figures **do not reproduce under either ceiling** and are superseded in place. The catalogue was found to be **mixing two ceilings** - the thirty-third cycle's size series is a $61m series and the plan of record carries $60.3m - so the size series is re-derived at $60.3m (60, 100, 137, 46, 206, 144, 147, 388, 488, 447) and the $61m series is retained for readability. The **boundary cross-check's sample rule is now fixed** (normalised full name as the only stable identifier, no symbol matching, collisions excluded, the venue's keyless top-500 screen as five pages of `per_page=100`, a single fixed date of 2026-10-20, the ratio as panel capitalisation over reference capitalisation, the median as the summary statistic, and the matched-name set reported alongside the ratio), and the re-derived pair is **estimated 0.9796 (n = 254, 100% within [0.5, 2]) and current 0.9931 (n = 38, 92.1% within [0.5, 2])**; the forty-eighth cycle's 0.9936 (n = 277) and 1.0021 (n = 44) do **not** reproduce, and its six estimated-metric outliers are an artefact of an unidentified matching rule - under exact normalised-name matching the estimated metric has **no outlier at all**. The consequence is material and is recorded in the plan of record: the disagreement between the two definitions' cross-checks is **largely a matching artefact, not a property of the two metrics**. None of this bears on the registered momentum-breakdown claim, so the mechanism (3/5), evidence-quality (2/5), robustness (1/5), net-value (1/5), falsifiability (4/5) and originality (2/5) dimensions are untouched and free-data accessibility remains 4/5. **The two carried placements are re-tested on their own terms.** Robustness 1/5 -> 2/5 (contribution 3 -> 6, **total 48 -> 51**): declined, and the ground is now **weaker** than the forty-eighth cycle recorded, because the cycle's census answers the underlying worry directly - the two metrics' strata differ in **membership** (the current metric's 84-asset common-panel stratum holds 100.00% median 30-day retention against the estimated metric's 95.24%) but not in **turnover rate** (1.18% of the median stratum a day against 1.14%), so the metric determination does not change how fast the population moves. It is nevertheless declined, because the metric still determines *which* population the conditional claim is conditioned on, and a robustness measurement of the comparison is not the same thing as a turnover measurement. Free-data accessibility 4/5 -> 5/5 (contribution 12 -> 15, **total 48 -> 51**): declined, and the cycle's finding now **cuts against it** - the community tier's panel is **revisable**, and the thirty-third cycle's exit decomposition did not reproduce from the same vendor on the same day, so the panel is not a point-in-time-stable input and cannot be described as a deep, dated, point-in-time screen. **The placement is recorded rather than dismissed.** The score-prose audit found no stale score in this entry's item 16 in any of the three places a dimension score can hide.

**Fifty-first cycle: no dimension moves; the total is 48, re-derived as 12+6+3+12+3+8+4, and the carried free-data disagreement is closed at 4/5.** The cycle's work was the read the forty-ninth cycle named as the highest-value next read, and it is now a completed read at the level the sources allow: the full text of SSRN 6648082 remains inaccessible (HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare interstitial on the abstract page, the PDF delivery endpoint and the DOI redirect), but the **complete** abstract and the **complete** twelve-item reference list are now on file from a free, dated route - Crossref's deposited metadata for the DOI - with the negative determinations recorded (OpenAlex indexes the metadata and not the text, `has_content: false` and a null `pdf_url`; Semantic Scholar has no record of the DOI; ResearchGate is request-only), so the entry's source is read as far as it can be read and no further. Reading it whole changes the *relation* between the paper and this entry without changing the entry: the paper's upper-tail nonlinearity, its two controls and its direction are all this entry's registered prediction, but its state variable is lagged and orthogonalised, its statistic is a horse-race regression of later momentum returns rather than the entry's registered difference of spreads, and its universe is the construct this entry replicates rather than the construct it claims - so a confirmation is written into the plan of record and the evidence-quality score stays at **2/5**, because this entry's registered statistic has still not been tested by anyone. The free-data score is decided at **4/5**: the community panel and the keyless screen both answer 200, the community API's missing-parameter behaviour is unchanged, and the historical market-capitalisation route is **narrower than the record stated** - the free tier serves a trailing 365-day window (401 with error 10012 outside it, 200 with a `market_data.market_cap` block inside it), which covers 366 of the panel's 2,850 dates and leaves the rest paid - so the reason changes and the score does not. The keyless screen's rule is tightened against a rate limit that answered 429 on two of five page requests today, because a truncated screen changes a capitalisation ratio's denominator. And the v1.11 clause's exit-decomposition triple is corrected in place: 5,740 and 5,783 are the entries counts, not the upward-migration counts. No dimension moves because none of this is evidence about the entry's registered prediction.

**Fifty-second cycle: no dimension moves; the total is 48, re-derived as 12+6+3+12+3+8+4.** The cycle's output is three things and none of them is evidence about the dispersion-to-momentum-spread mapping. (i) **The paper's result is reached, through a dated third-party route that was not on file.** A research newsletter's recap published **2026-04-28** - three days after the paper's last revision - reports that the paper finds **"the dispersion of returns across coins predicts momentum breakdowns better than Bitcoin volatility"**, that **"in extreme dispersion regimes, momentum weakened sharply"**, and that a dispersion-scaled implementation raised the **Sharpe ratio from 0.63 to 0.80** and cut the **maximum drawdown from -42.5% to -17.1%**. This is a **secondary** read and is classified as one: the paper itself remains access 2 (abstract, plus a dated third-party characterisation of its result), because the publisher's own server answers 403 on every route and RePEc's IDEAS route returns 404. It is nonetheless the first evidence the catalogue has that the paper reports an **implementation** and not only a regression, and it is a **specification constraint** on the entry rather than a replication of it: the paper's statistic is a **lagged, orthogonalised cross-sectional dispersion of returns** in a **horse-race regression** against **Bitcoin realised volatility** and **average cross-asset correlation**, and the entry's registered statistic is a **difference of spreads**. **The paper's own regression - sample, estimator, coefficients, robustness - is still unread**, and the cycle says so rather than implying the third-party summary closes the item. (ii) **The trailing-365-day free market-capitalisation route is put to work, and the panel's final year is cross-checked against the community series.** On **48** matched cells (8 assets x 6 dates over 2025-10-21 to 2026-10-20) the two free sources agree closely - **48 of 48 (100%)** within [0.5, 2], **median ratio 0.9982**, **44 of 48 (91.7%)** within [0.9, 1.1], per-asset medians between **0.9909 and 1.0010** - but the disagreement is **date-level rather than asset-level**, with per-date medians running from **0.9855** to **1.1023**. The consequence is written into the plan: **the boundary cross-check is a ratio evaluated at a single fixed date, and it must be quoted with its date, its source and its per-date dispersion**; on the plan's own fixed date, 2026-10-20, the cross-source median is **0.9809**, well inside the acceptance band, so the check's existing conclusion is unaffected. The **free-data accessibility score is held at 4/5** and is not raised, because the route still cannot carry the other **2,484** of the panel's 2,850 dates and the residual gap is about the panel's revisability, not about a paywall. (iii) **The keyless tier's rate-limit behaviour is measured and the retry policy is written.** A burst of 40 unauthenticated calls answers **200** for the first **4** and **429** for the remaining **36**; the 429 carries a **`retry-after`** header (observed **18** and **60** seconds) and the tier returns **no** `x-ratelimit-*` headers at all, so the client cannot compute its own budget; the burst is restored after about **70 seconds** of idleness; and at one call every 5 seconds the tier serves **6 calls** in the first 30 seconds and then throttles continuously, so the burst capacity is of the order of **five to six calls** and the sustained rate of the order of **five to six per minute**. The fifty-first cycle's "a retry with a delay" is replaced by a policy with numbers in it: **honour `retry-after`, floor the wait at 10 seconds and cap it at 60; wait at least 9 seconds after every 200; reject the screen outright if any page is not 200 after the policy has been applied; record every page's status, the retry count and the total sleep**. A pull under that policy completed **48 of 48** cells with **6** 429s absorbed and **360** seconds slept, with no cell lost. **No dimension moves**, because a source read, a cross-source comparison of two free market-capitalisation series and a rate-limit measurement are all construction and access facts, and the standing rule keeps them on the construction and access side of the ledger.
**Fifty-third cycle: no dimension moves; the total is 48, re-derived as 12+6+3+12+3+8+4.** The cycle's work on this entry was to get as close to the paper's method as free and dated routes allow, and to register a claim-side source. The paper's **nine** resolvable references were identified and read as a partial read of its method, and three things follow that bear on how the entry must be reported: the paper's Sharpe ratios are **deflated** Sharpe ratios (it cites Bailey 2014), so its headline **0.63 to 0.80** is already selection-adjusted; its implementation is a **state-scaled long-only book** in the Barroso-Santa-Clara / Moreira-Muir lineage, which is a **different object** from this entry's registered **difference of cross-sectional spreads** and therefore not a replication target for it; and one of its two named controls - average cross-asset correlation - rests on a single non-peer-reviewed working paper. The next question is therefore no longer a construction question but a **comparative one**, and it is stated as three parts. (i) *Which state variable is operative, and is the entry's claim wrong or merely not the operative variable?* The eleventh cycle's answer so far: the dispersion variable has no independent published test at all; the volatility-regime and average-pairwise-correlation variables have both been tested on comparable coin-level panels, the latter directly and with a null result on the co-movement mechanism; and the cross-asset dependence structure is itself non-stationary with an undated sign flip, which is a further reason that a single "state variable" framing may be the wrong object. The highest-value remaining external work is to find whether **any** independent party has tested a *dispersion* state variable against a cross-sectional crypto signal, and if not, to decide whether the entry should be reframed from "dispersion is the operative variable" to "cross-sectional signal reliability is state-dependent and the operative variable is not yet identified" - which would be a **narrowing to a better-identified claim**, and would require the failed claim to be explicitly withdrawn under the falsification-handling rule. That reframing is *not* performed in this cycle, because the entry's registered prediction has not been tested and failed, so the rule is not engaged and the entry is not re-specified. (ii) *Does the base effect survive a free, point-in-time, cost-aware construction on a perpetual universe?* This is the question the catalogue's Arefev and H72 results bear on adversely, and the eleventh cycle's new survivorship-aware evidence (arXiv:2510.14435v4) bears on favourably but on a different universe; the honest position is that the answer is *unsettled and universe-dependent*, and a free replication must report which universe it used. (iii) *Is the archive's futures tree versioned at all?* The eleventh cycle established that the published update log covers the spot tree and that the log is not exhaustive as published, so the versioning status of the futures tree - the tree this entry and the other two active entries actually use - is unestablished. A cheap, decisive check remains open: enumerate the `updates/` directory in the binance-public-data repository and search its artefacts for futures paths, and record the result. 17. Next most valuable research question: can any *free, dated, point-in-time* construction of a crypto universe bound the delisting half of survivorship - that is, is there a free source of historical circulating supply, historical market capitalisation, or a dated delisting record for tokens that a major venue has delisted, that would let a market-cap screen be built retrospectively rather than reconstructed from volume alone? This is a data-availability question with a binary answer and no performance calculation attached, and it is the single question that decides whether this entry, or a successor to it, is testable at all under the free-data standard. Two subsidiary questions follow if the answer is yes: does the published dispersion-momentum state-dependence survive on a universe with a market-cap screen that is honest in both directions, and does it add anything over a Bitcoin-realized-volatility state variable? If the answer to the first question is no, the correct outcome is a recorded deferral of the whole cross-sectional-survivorship-aware family rather than a repeated re-specification of it. The same data blocker also binds the second non-derivatives family examined in this cycle - predictable token supply changes - whose published result is strong and whose essential input (historical circulating supply and vesting schedules) is blocked by the same CoinGecko free-tier history restriction, so a single answer to the data question would unblock or retire both families at once. **Ninth-cycle answer to the first question: yes, for the delisting half.** A dated delisting record for tokens a major venue has delisted is constructible on free data, by derivation rather than by a vendor field: the Binance public data archive keeps a dated daily kline file for every USD-M perpetual symbol ever listed, and the terminal file of a ceased contract carries volume=0 and trade count=0 with a frozen close, so the last trading date is exactly the last file with a non-zero trade count. The construction is validated against the venue's own announcements (LUNA 2022-05-13; OMG 2025-01-31 after two postponements) and against one re-listing (CVC), and the two hazards - an incomplete monthly tree and re-listings - are recorded in item 10. The *other* half of the data question is unchanged and still negative: historical circulating supply, historical market capitalisation and market-cap rank remain not confirmed free on any free tier, so the token-dilution family stays deferred and the published market-cap screen must be substituted rather than reproduced. **The next most valuable research question is therefore no longer the data question.** It is: on the now-constructible survivorship-aware perpetual universe, does the momentum spread really differ between high- and low-dispersion states, and does the answer survive the fact that the base spread does not itself survive costs? Concretely, the test must (i) fix the universe rule, the dispersion definition, the momentum specification, the state variable and all thresholds before any data is inspected; (ii) report the *difference of spreads* between the high- and low-dispersion states, not the level of either spread, so that a null base effect does not make the question unanswerable; (iii) report the conditional spread net of costs alongside the gross, given Arefev's finding; (iv) include the two mandatory controls (Bitcoin realized volatility and average pairwise cross-asset correlation) and the liquidity-filter control; and (v) use heavy-tail inference - block bootstrap with the cross-section kept intact within blocks, median-based summaries, the volatility of the signal bucket reported alongside the mean difference, and no Sharpe ratio. If the difference of spreads is null once the base spread is known to be cost-negative, the correct outcome is a rejection of the entry, not another re-specification, because the entry's registered prediction will then have been tested on a free, survivorship-aware universe. **Tenth-cycle replacement of the question.** The data question is closed, and the specification is fixed, so the highest-value question is no longer *whether the entry can be tested* but *which state variable is operative* - because a published peer-reviewed source now treats a market-wide regime as the operative variable for cross-sectional crypto signal reliability while finding the co-movement mechanism unsupported, and a second peer-reviewed source finds crypto momentum itself to arise only in UP-UP state transitions. The binding question is therefore: **on the free, survivorship-aware perpetual universe, does the dispersion state variable explain any of the variance in the momentum spread that a Bitcoin-realized-volatility state and a pairwise-correlation state do not already explain?** Concretely, the validation must estimate the difference of spreads under three competing state variables - dispersion, correlation and Bitcoin realized volatility - on the same universe, the same momentum specification and the same inference, and report them side by side, with dispersion's incremental content reported as the residual. If the dispersion state adds nothing over the correlation state, the entry is not wrong, it is *not the operative variable*, and the correct outcome is a rewrite of the mechanism rather than a rejection. Two subsidiary questions follow and are recorded for the next cycle. (a) **The delisting sign.** The entry is long winners and short losers, and delisted tokens are disproportionately losers, so the short leg has a mechanical advantage that is not an edge; the closest preregistered prior art states that the *sign* of the delisting bias on a short-perp book through exactly these events is unknown, so the entry's headline must be reported both including and excluding delisted tokens and neither may be presented as the answer. (b) **The venue announcement feed.** The tenth cycle could not confirm whether a free, dated, machine-readable venue announcement feed exists, because Binance's public REST API returns HTTP 451 from this research environment ("service unavailable from a restricted location") and its announcement pages are behind a WAF human-verification gate; this is an environment limitation and not a data-availability determination, it leaves the delisting-announcement question open, and it does not change this entry, whose universe is built from the archive rather than from announcements.
**Thirteenth-cycle update: the question has changed from "is the dispersion variable the operative one?" to "what does a free replication of the published construction actually estimate?".** The eleventh cycle established that the dispersion variable has no independent published test while the volatility-regime and average-pairwise-correlation variables do, and that the dependence structure is itself non-stationary. The thirteenth cycle adds three facts that reframe the question. (i) **A third party has already published a replication of the entry's own construction**, in executable form, including the rival state variables (Bitcoin realized volatility over 30 days and average off-diagonal correlation over 60 days) and the dispersion overlay; so the *ordering* of state variables in the published construction is no longer an open question about the literature, and what remains open is whether a **free** replication — with the market-capitalisation screen replaced by listing age and trailing volume — reproduces that ordering, on a *different universe* and, if the size-momentum lead is right, on a *different size composition*. (ii) **The base is now documented in a peer-reviewed source as close to non-existent**, with many cross-sectional momentum portfolios liquidated and those with significant mean returns often earning negative profits, so a free replication that fails to find the conditional effect may be failing because the unconditional spread is not there, not because the conditional switch is not there — and the plan must therefore estimate the unconditional spread on the *same free universe* as the conditional effect, or the comparison is uninterpretable. (iii) **The size-composition confound is a new and specific threat**: if the momentum sign differs by size quintile, then the free screen (age and volume) and the published screen (market capitalisation) select different populations with different signs, and the entry's registered claim may be about a population that a free replication cannot construct.
**The highest-value next question is therefore now a construction question with a specific failure mode:** on a free, dated, survivorship-aware universe, does the *unconditional* cross-sectional momentum spread exist at all, and if it exists, is the dispersion overlay's conditional increment distinguishable from the unconditional spread net of costs — with the size composition of the free universe reported alongside, so that a null result can be attributed to the wrong population rather than to the wrong switch? That question is decidable on free data, it does not require the paid tier, and it is a precondition for the entry's registered claim ever being testable. The lead recorded for the next cycle is to verify the size-momentum source properly (Xu and Wu) and to establish whether the free screen's size composition can be measured at all, since historical market capitalisation is unavailable free and the entry's universe may therefore be non-reconstructible in the dimension that matters most.

**Fourteenth-cycle update: the lead is discharged, and the question it was attached to is now decidable.** The lead — "verify the size-momentum source properly (Xu and Wu)" — **is discharged**: the source is located and dated (SSRN 6628860, 1 January 2026, a working-paper preprint), its numbers are confirmed, and two stronger sources corroborate the same size-dependence of the sign. The second half of the lead — "establish whether the free screen's size composition can be measured at all" — is now partly answered, and the answer is a determination: **historical market capitalisation is not free and dated** (CoinGecko's free tier refuses every historical query with HTTP 401 and its chart endpoint returns HTTP 404; the entry's own eleventh-cycle determination, re-confirmed), so the free screen's size composition **cannot be measured directly**; what can be measured on free data is a **proxy** for it — listing age and trailing quote volume — and the two are related but not identical, because a coin can be old and liquid and still small, or young and thin and large. That leaves three questions, in order of value. (i) **Is there any free, dated, point-in-time source for market capitalisation or circulating supply that the catalogue has not already ruled out?** The thirteenth cycle's answer was no for the obvious candidates, and the fourteenth cycle adds one more to the list: the venue's own contract metadata (the archive's `exchangeInfo` history and the announcement feed) carries no market capitalisation, and the *only* free route to a market-cap series the catalogue has found is a **current-only** one, so a point-in-time size label is likely to remain unobtainable free — which would make the size-matched control a *proxy* control, and a validator would have to say that. (ii) **What is the free screen's size composition, in the proxy sense, relative to the published screen's?** A validator can compute the free screen's age and volume distribution on the free data and compare it to the $1bn-market-cap screen's composition *as of the current date*, and a large divergence is a prediction that the free replication's base spread will differ in sign from the published one — a testable, cheap, and *falsifiable* preliminary that does not require the paid tier and that can be run before the entry's own test. (iii) **Does the entry's switch survive within a size stratum?** If the momentum spread is estimated within the largest available stratum of the free screen — where the base sign is documented to be positive — the entry's registered comparison becomes interpretable, and the price of the restriction is a smaller universe and a different state variable's distribution, which must be reported. These three are the next cycle's most valuable work on this entry, and they are all *constructive* rather than confirmatory, which is the right posture for an entry whose registered claim has never been tested and whose base has been documented three times to be sign-fragile.

**Twenty-third-cycle update to this entry's open question: the question is no longer whether a size measure exists, but which metric defines the stratum, and how much the stratum churns.** (i) *Which metric defines the stratum?* The current and estimated panels disagree by a factor of three at the panel's own 20th percentile and asset by asset, and the base effect's sign is documented to depend on size composition, so the choice of metric is not cosmetic: it decides which population the entry's conditional claim is about. The specification must fix one metric, declare the other as a robustness check, and state the boundary cross-check statistic for each (this cycle's: median panel-to-reference ratio 0.97 estimated, 0.98 current). (ii) *What is the small stratum's composition by date, and how much does it churn?* The cycle measured the count - 61 assets below $61m in mid-2019, 450 today - but not the churn, and churn is the binding measurement for a within-stratum comparison: if the small stratum's membership is largely different assets in each year, a within-stratum comparison across the window is not a comparison of the same population over time, and the specification must state whether the comparison is cross-sectional-per-date (recommended) or pooled. (iii) *Is the membership ground the right one to hold the free-data score at 4/5?* A reader could argue that a 901-asset point-in-time market-cap panel with a populated small stratum throughout 2019-2026 is enough for the entry's own construction, and that the published screen's membership is a *benchmark* rather than an input - in which case the free-data dimension should rise to 5/5 and the total to 51. The cycle declines the move and records the reason: the entry's registered prediction is a *conditional* claim about a *base effect whose sign is documented to depend on the size composition of the universe*, and the only instrument that ties the free panel to the published evidence is the membership comparison, so a free replication without it is a test of a different population's claim. **The alternative placement (free-data 5/5, total 51) is recorded rather than dismissed.**
**Twenty-eighth-cycle update: the question is no longer whether the stratum churns, but what the churn does to the entry's identification.** The twentieth-seventh cycle left the question as "which metric defines the stratum, and how much does it churn". The churn is now measured: at a 30-day lag the median 95.5% of a date's small stratum is still below $61m, the 10th percentile is 79.4% and the minimum 44.3%, while the panel's own membership is essentially unchanged — so the churn is **price movement across the size boundary plus data stopping, not panel turnover**. The question that replaces it is the construction one the entry has always needed: **must the size stratum be re-formed point-in-time on every date, with a declared missing-observation treatment for assets whose series stops, and is the published screen's current-only membership a confound that no free construction can remove?** The cycle's answer to the second half is that it cannot be removed on free data, and the answer to the first half is yes, with three clauses the cycle measured: the stablecoin exclusion must be a stated rule (composition moves day to day), the panel-to-reference cross-check must be matched on a stable identifier (ticker matching manufactures 80x divergences out of symbol collisions), and an asset whose market cap crosses the boundary remains a member of the universe but a different stratum member from that date — so the stratum must be **re-cut**, not merely re-ranked.

**Thirty-second-cycle amendment (2026-10-21) — no dimension moves; the total is 48, re-derived as 12+6+3+12+3+8+4, and the turnover measurement is extended from one stratum to the whole size spectrum and decomposed into survival, band-retention and migration.** (i) *The extension.* The catalogue's turnover measurement was confined to the single sub-$61m stratum. This cycle measured the **lag-overlap profile in five size bands** (<$10m, $10m–$61m, $61m–$250m, $250m–$1bn, >$1bn) at lags of 1, 7, 30, 90 and **180** days (the 180-day lag is new), and **decomposed** every band profile into **survival** (the member is still in the panel at t+L), **band-retention** (still in the panel *and* still inside the same band) and **migration** (the difference). **The result changes the picture the catalogue had: churn is not monotonic in size.** Median 30-day band-retention is **90.4%** (<$10m), **88.7%** ($10m–$61m), **83.8%** ($61m–$250m), **83.1%** ($250m–$1bn) and **95.7%** (>$1bn) — the **middle** bands turn over fastest and the smallest band is among the most stable, because an asset in the smallest band can only leave it by *growing*. Survival is **~100% at the median in every band at 30 and 90 days**, so the retention loss is migration across a size boundary rather than the panel dropping assets; at 180 days the median migration is 23.8% (<$10m), 29.4% ($10m–$61m), 38.3% ($61m–$250m), 40.0% ($250m–$1bn) and 12.2% (>$1bn). (ii) *The exit accounting answers the twenty-eighth cycle's open question with a number.* Over the **2,824 daily transitions** of the sub-$61m stratum, exits run at a **median of 1.0 per day** (mean 1.87, maximum 23) and **67.2%** of days lose at least one member; of the **5,292** exits, **96.3% are upward price migrations** past $61m and only **3.7% (194) are panel deaths**. The twenty-eighth cycle's recorded conclusion — "the churn is price movement across the size boundary plus data stopping, not panel turnover" — is therefore **quantified: it is 96.3% price movement and 3.7% data stopping**. The identification consequence is sharp and is recorded as a specification requirement: the stratum's membership change is a **systematic composition gradient** (assets graduate upward), so a *pooled* comparison across dates would confound the entry's signal with that gradient, and the cross-sectional-per-date construction the catalogue already recommends is now the **only** construction consistent with the measured composition dynamics. (iii) *Boundary sensitivity.* The recorded sub-boundary profile is **not** an artefact of the $61m cut: median 30-day retention is **94.3%** (<$46m), **95.3%** (<$61m), **96.6%** (<$100m) and **98.0%** (<$250m) — a 3.7pp spread across a 5.4x range of boundaries. The catalogue's recorded 95.5% at 30 days for the whole sub-$61m stratum is reproduced at 95.3%. (iv) *The boundary cross-check re-run with stable-identifier matching*, against a reference screen re-fetched live on 2026-10-21 (CoinGecko's keyless tier, which **clamps `per_page` at 100** — a fact that must be recorded, because the screen must be paginated in 100-row pages and a single large request silently returns fewer rows than asked for): **364 stable-identifier matches** on normalised full name, **265** of them comparable at the panel's final date (2026-10-20), giving a panel-to-reference median ratio of **0.9997** (p10 0.9801, p90 1.0135, **264 of 265 within [0.5, 2]**). The single outlier is again an identifier artefact (`mpl` matched to the reference row named *Syrup*, ratio 0.016). Inside the **$10m–$400m** band the agreement is tighter (n = 169, median 0.9997, p10 0.9743, p90 1.0147, min 0.8324, max 1.0646), and the current-metric panel (135 assets) again shows the two recorded supply-definition outliers (`gno` 3.79x, `xlm` 2.98x). The reference screen's own size profile was re-verified at **rank 100 $637.6m, rank 200 $169.3m, rank 300 $94.4m, rank 400 $62.0m, rank 500 $46.5m** (prior cycle: $630.9m / $170.4m / $91.7m / $61.3m / $46.1m), so the $61m boundary remains the rank-400 level. The twenty-eighth cycle's recorded **median 0.998 over 277 matched names** is reproduced (0.9997 over 265), and its methodological rule — *match on a stable identifier and drop colliding symbols* — is re-confirmed as the method. (v) *Panel state at the cycle's date.* The community panel's final date is **2026-10-20** (no 2026-10-21 row is published yet), with **722 of 850** assets live and **128 dead (15.06%)**, of which **119** had entered the sub-$61m stratum at some point; the live sub-$61m stratum is **449** names. Band composition has drifted materially across the panel's life (136 assets in mid-2019 → 722 now; the <$10m band 17 → 170 and the $61m–$250m band 38 → 127), so a stratum re-formed point-in-time is a *changing population*, which the measured migration profile now quantifies. **No dimension moves**, and the reason is the standing rule: these are construction and population measurements of a confound control, and they bear on the entry's registered dispersion-conditional momentum claim nowhere; the free-data ground that holds the score at 4/5 — the free screen's small stratum is a *different population* from the published screen's, and the published screen's membership is current-only — is untouched by anything measured here. The alternative placements (free-data 5/5 → 51; free-data 3/5 → 45) remain recorded rather than dismissed.

**Thirty-third-cycle amendment (2026-10-21) — no dimension moves; the total is 48, re-derived as 12+6+3+12+3+8+4; the composition gradient is measured directly rather than by inference, the stablecoin rule is shown to be immaterial to it, and the panel is shown to answer the reference screen's historical-membership question approximately.** (i) **The per-date stratum re-formed point-in-time is reproduced and the graduation rate is now a measured quantity rather than an exit decomposition.** The sub-$61m stratum's size on the dates sampled is 60 (2019-07-01), 100 (2020-01-01), 138 (2021-01-01), **47 (2022-01-01)**, 208 (2023-01-01), 144 (2024-01-01), 150 (2025-01-01), 388 (2026-01-01), 491 (2026-08-01) and **449 (2026-10-20)**, with a median of 145, a maximum of 492 and **all 2,850 panel dates populated** — the twenty-eighth and thirty-second cycles' counts are reproduced to the digit. Over the 2,849 daily transitions there are **5,098 upward exits, 5,286 downward entries and 225 panel deaths**, so **95.8% of the 5,323 exits are upward price migrations and 4.2% are panel deaths**, reproducing the recorded 96.3% / 3.7%. The **forward** graduation rate is now measured directly: **6.1%** of the stratum's members are above the boundary 30 days later (sampled every 7 days, 66,195 member-date observations), against a pooled 30-day retention of **93.2%**, and the median daily upward exit rate is **1.79 exits per day, 1.23% of the median stratum per day** — so the composition gradient is *slow* on any single day and *large* over a month, which is the number the entry's within-stratum comparison has to be robust to. (ii) **The stablecoin-exclusion rule is measured, and it is immaterial to the turnover measurement.** A **stated list rule** (20 pegged tickers) removes **4 of the 449** live sub-$61m members — `busd` ($34.4m), `gusd` ($36.1m), `pax` ($23.6m), `ageur` ($1.4m) — leaving 445, and the 30-day retention is **93.1%** against 93.2% unexcluded. A **data-driven peg detector** (90-day market-cap coefficient of variation below 5%) flags 39 assets, 12 of them in the stratum, leaving 437 and a retention of **93.0%** — but the two rules disagree in both directions: the detector's stratum members include **10 assets that are not stablecoins** (mostly fan tokens whose prices are stale, so a "pegged" market cap confounds a peg with an illiquid quote) and miss two that are (`pax`, `ageur`). **The rule choice moves the stratum's membership by 1.3% and leaves the turnover measurement indistinguishable, so the rule is a disclosed choice rather than a binding constraint — and the cycle records the failure mode of the data-driven alternative, because a validator who substitutes it for the list rule will be filtering on illiquidity.** (iii) **The panel does cover the reference screen's historical-membership question, approximately and better than the catalogue had recorded.** The reference screen's bottom-quintile threshold today is **$46.67m** (rank 500, re-verified). Against that fixed threshold, **785 of the 850** panel assets have at some point carried a market cap at or above it; **562 of the 722** live panel assets have at some point been in the sub-$61m stratum; and **525 of the 722 have graduated from below $61m to at least $46.7m** — so the set of assets that have occupied the published screen's bottom band is far larger than the screen's present membership, the free panel can enumerate it, and the entry's "graduating population" problem is confirmed in its sharpest form: **the screen's current membership is a survivorship-selected sample of a much larger population that has passed through its size band.** (iv) **The boundary cross-check was re-run** against a live reference screen with a name-then-unique-symbol matching rule: **376 stable-identifier matches of 500 rows, 287 comparable on the panel's final date, median ratio 0.9986** (p10 0.9766, p90 1.0126; 283/287 within [0.5, 2]), reproducing the thirty-second cycle's 0.9997 on a different matching rule; the panel's final date is still **2026-10-20**, so the panel has not advanced and the recorded cross-check stands. The four outliers are again identifier artefacts (`cusd` → *cap-usd* 0.17, `gusd` 0.24, `chip` → *usdai* 0.34, `mew` 0.83). The reference screen's size profile is re-verified at ranks 100/200/300/400/500 = **$638.9m / $169.3m / $94.5m / $62.1m / $46.7m**. (v) **No dimension moves.** These are population and construction measurements of a confound control and bear on the entry's registered dispersion-conditional momentum claim nowhere; the free-data ground that holds the score at 4/5 — the free screen's small stratum is a *different population* from the published screen's, and the published screen's membership is current-only — is untouched. The alternative placements (free-data 5/5 → 51; free-data 3/5 → 45) remain recorded rather than dismissed.

**Thirty-sixth-cycle amendment (2026-10-21) — no dimension moves; the total is 48, re-derived as 12+6+3+12+3+8+4; the market-cap definition is pre-registered and the substituted screens' composition is declared.** (i) *Market-cap definition pre-registered.* The free screen's small stratum is metric-determined: under `CapMrktEstUSD` the free screen has 447 assets below the reference ceiling ($60.3m bottom-quintile ceiling) of which 405 are absent from the reference screen, while under `CapMrktCurUSD` it has only 32 of which 28 are absent; the two strata intersect on 22 assets (Jaccard 0.048). A free replication must therefore state which market-cap definition it uses before any within-stratum comparison, and the pre-registered definition is `CapMrktEstUSD` (the estimated, supply-estimated metric on 850 assets), with `CapMrktCurUSD` (the current, circulating-supply-based metric on 135 assets) declared as the robustness check. The boundary cross-check statistic (median panel-to-reference ratio) must be reported for each metric separately (0.97 estimated, 0.98 current for correctly matched names), and the choice of metric must be fixed before the stratum is re-cut point-in-time on every date. (ii) *Substituted screens' composition declared.* Because historical market capitalisation is not free, the entry substitutes listing-age and trailing-volume screens: a symbol becomes eligible only after 90 days of trading history; the universe is the top 40 by trailing 30-day quote volume, reselected every 90 days; a symbol leaves when its trailing volume rank falls out of the top 60. The same metric-determination argument applies to the substituted screens: their own size composition must be declared alongside every within-stratum comparison, because listing age and trailing volume select on a different axis from market capitalisation and may select populations whose base momentum spread has a different sign (small coins reverse, large coins continue, per the documented size-momentum structure). The free screen's size composition — its age distribution, its trailing-volume distribution, and its overlap with the published market-cap screen's strata — must be reported as a replication limitation, not suppressed. The reference screen's current-only membership remains a stated confound; it can be benchmarked against only as of the check date, not historically. No dimension moves: these are specification and replication-limitation declarations, and none bears on the registered dispersion-conditional momentum claim. **Forty-seventh-cycle note (2026-10-21) — the metric-sensitivity question becomes separable, and the next step is now a measurement rather than a declaration.** (i) Run the **within-asset metric comparison** on the newly identified **84-asset common panel** — the assets that carry both `CapMrktEstUSD` and `CapMrktCurUSD` — on a **per-asset common window**, because on only 19 of the 84 do the two metrics begin on the same date; report each asset's value under both definitions and the resulting change in its stratum membership, and report it beside the **population-composition** statistic across the disjoint remainder, so that the metric's effect on the *measured value* is separated from its effect on *which assets are in the stratum*. (ii) Report the boundary cross-check **per metric** (0.97 estimated, 0.98 current) and the substituted screens' own size composition beside every within-stratum comparison. (iii) The entry's substantive question is unchanged and remains a **return statistic**: does the base effect survive costs on the free panel, and does the dispersion switch change it? — which the catalogue does not compute here and which the entry's plan now specifies as a validation action elsewhere.
**Forty-eighth-cycle amendment (2026-10-21) — no dimension moves; the total is 48, re-derived as 12+6+3+12+3+8+4; the within-asset metric comparison is executed, and the binding question changes from *which market-cap definition to use* to *how the free replication's population is made to match the published screen's population at all*.** The forty-seventh cycle's binding question was the metric choice; it is now answered by measurement — the definition decides the stratum on **4.77%** of asset-days and on **44 of 83** assets at some point, and the two definitions select **disjoint** small populations wherever only one is available. The question that now binds is the one that measurement exposed: **the published screen is a live ranking of the top 500 by *current* market capitalisation, and the free panel's small stratum is a dated, point-in-time population that the published screen never had** — 406 of the 450 sub-$61m assets in the estimated panel are absent from the reference top 500 altogether, and the panel's own composition churns. A validator therefore cannot replicate the published screen's membership on free data at any historical date, and the highest-value next measurement is the one that would make the replication's own population **point-in-time-correct against a stated definition**: a **stratum-membership census on the free panel over the registered horizon** — for each date in the entry's window, the number of assets below the ceiling under each metric, the **entry and exit** of assets across that boundary, and the **turnover rate** of the small stratum under each metric, with stablecoin and deprecated-token membership declared per date — because the binding measurement for a within-stratum conditional claim is the **stability of the stratum it conditions on**, and the catalogue has measured the stratum's *size* and *composition* at one date but never its *churn*. That census is a composition and count measurement, not a return statistic, and it can be executed on the free panel without any performance figure. A second, smaller item: the **boundary cross-check must be re-derivable from a dated, reproducible sample**, and the cycle's re-derivation shows the recorded 0.97 / 0.98 pair is not reproducible from today's matched names while the outlier set is; the check therefore needs a fixed sample rule (match on stable identifier, exclude collisions, fix the date) before it is quoted again.

Corrected in place. **The generalisation of the twenty-third and thirty-second cycles' rules: an audit of the score prose must check the prose's tense, because a narrative correctly attributed to its own cycle can still assert a present-tense fact that has since changed.**
- **The venue's own file-index route is the standing method for enumerating a vendor's dated products, and using it overturns a recorded coverage limit.** `GET /api/v5/public/market-data-history?module={M}&instType={T}&instFamilyList={F}&dateAggrType=daily&begin={ms}&end={ms}` (keyless, access 1, at most ten days per call for the daily aggregation) returns, for each module, the list of dated archive files with their URLs. The catalogue had never called it, and it discloses the funding archive the recorded 315-day hole was built on. The modules are 1 (tick-by-tick trades), 2 (1-minute candlesticks), 3 (funding rate, swaps only), 4 (400-level L2 order book), 5 (5000-level L2 order book), 6 (50-level order book, options), 11 (borrowing rate) — **there is no liquidation module**, so the venue-wide "no dated liquidation product" determination is **strengthened** by a test that does not depend on path guessing at all, and three further dated products are disclosed: the L2 depth archives (the 400-level book for BTC-USDT-SWAP begins **2026-06-09** and runs to 2026-10-20; the 5000-level book begins later), and the all-swap / all-futures / all-spot tick and 1-minute candlestick archives.
- **CRYPTO-EDGE-003 — the recorded 315-day funding hole is superseded in place, the funding history is continuous for 2,119 days, and the legacy archive's timestamp column is a live construction hazard.** The full statement is in the entry's item 16. In summary: the union of the legacy per-instrument daily product (2021-01-01 → 2025-09-07) and the newly found all-swap daily product (2022-01-17 → 2026-10-20, plus a 30-day island in September 2021) is **one continuous interval with zero interior holes**; the per-instrument settlement streams are **99.8% complete**; the legacy product's `funding_time` column is the *next period's* timestamp, so it is displaced from the settlement instant by **one funding interval, which differs by instrument** (8h, 4h, 2h or 1h), and the two products also partition the settlement stream differently, so a date-keyed join double-counts and misses settlements; and the entry's symmetric liquidity filter is executable **one-sided on 729 dates and two-sided on 617** of the 1,346-day window, with the publisher's leg complete on every date and the second venue's leg present from 2023-12-31.
- **CRYPTO-EDGE-001 — the prospective arm's denominator is characterised to the contract, and the contemporaneity mismatch is quantified.** The live per-contract denominator is **786 contracts** (514 swaps, 272 dated futures) plus an option book of 7,872 contracts of which 79.0% carry zero open interest; the dated per-instrument history covers **782 of 786 (99.6%)**, the four exceptions being three newly listed dated futures (code 51001, together **0.33%** of the BTC aggregate open interest and **0.22%** of the ETH aggregate) and one test instrument. The route's 24-hour densities reproduce (ETH 2,047, BTC 1,131, SOL 499, PEPE 489, XRP 175, inverse 6) and its **time-clustering is quantified**: the busiest decile of hours holds 35-67% of a day's events and a single hour can hold 44.9% of a family's. The **contemporaneity mismatch** between a 24-hour event window and the daily denominator is **0.0-24.0 hours of window-centre displacement (mean 12.1)**, with the matching denominator row covering on average only **11.9 of the 24 event hours** — so a daily-cadence denominator is not contemporaneous with a rolling 24-hour numerator unless the request is aligned to the 16:00 UTC bucket boundary.
- **The two open-interest products' daily rows do not have the same aggregation semantics, and this is the reason a naive reconciliation fails.** The **aggregate** 1D row is *identical* to the aggregate 1H row at the same stamp (0.0000% on every date tested) — an end-of-window snapshot. The **per-contract** 1D row matches neither the 1H value at the same stamp (-1.9% to +3.3%) nor the mean of the preceding 24 hourly values (-0.9% to +5.0%), and the vendor documents neither. Consequently a venue-level total built from the per-contract **daily** series does **not** reconcile with the aggregate 1D route: over 100 overlapping dates the residuals run **median -1.61% (BTC), -1.29% (ETH), +0.96% (SOL)** with tails of **-7.42%/+6.92%, -9.95%/+11.41% and -9.15%/+23.13%**. When the semantics are matched — the per-contract **1H** values at the aggregate's stamp, summed — the reconciliation is tight: **+0.09% to +1.76% (BTC, 11 contracts), +0.22% to +0.88% (ETH, 12), -0.02% to +0.94% (SOL, 7)**. **The two products are the same book; the daily route's residual is a semantic difference, not a scope difference**, and any validator who reconciles a per-contract daily total against the aggregate daily route will mistake one for the other.
- **The per-instrument daily open-interest product's breadth is now measured across the whole venue, and it is nearly complete.** A sweep of every live instrument (786) finds **782 carrying a daily series**; only **114** reach the product's floor of 2023-12-31, the rest starting at their own listing date (443 start on the listing date, 198 one day before it because the daily row is stamped 16:00 UTC of the preceding day, and 14 one day after it). **Only 23 of the 782 have missing days inside their covered window**, and 14 of those are missing exactly one day at the listing boundary while the other 9 are dated futures with multi-week gaps (up to 62 days). Every series ends on the same date, 2026-10-20. The publisher's own per-contract daily metrics archive was measured in parallel: **1,038 of 1,039** USDⓈ-M symbols carry a daily series, with 18 symbols stopping at 2025-03-10 and 14 at 2023-06-13 — the delisted and expired dated contracts — so the publisher's leg has its own interior coverage holes, which the entry's delisting-exclusion rule must cover.
- **CRYPTO-EDGE-004 — the composition gradient is measured directly, the stablecoin rule is shown immaterial to it, and the panel is shown to answer the reference screen's historical-membership question.** The per-date stratum reproduces to the digit (60 / 100 / 138 / **47** / 208 / 144 / 150 / 388 / 491 / **449**; median 145; all 2,850 dates populated); **95.8% of the 5,323 exits are upward price migrations and 4.2% panel deaths**; the **forward** 30-day graduation rate is **6.1%** and the daily upward exit rate **1.23% of the median stratum**. The stablecoin rule is measured three ways — no rule (449 members, 93.2% retention), a stated list of 20 pegged tickers (445, 93.1%) and a data-driven 90-day peg detector (437, 93.0%) — and the **rule is immaterial to the turnover measurement**, while the detector is shown to confound pegs with illiquidity. The panel can reconstruct the reference screen's historical membership approximately and better than recorded: **785 of 850** assets have ever exceeded today's $46.67m bottom-quintile threshold, **562 of 722** live assets have been in the sub-$61m stratum, and **525 of 722 have graduated from below $61m to at least $46.7m**. The boundary cross-check re-run on a different matching rule gives a **median ratio of 0.9986** (376 matches, 287 comparable) against the recorded 0.9997, with the panel's final date still 2026-10-20.
- **Adversarial review.** All three carried disagreements re-tested and **upheld**: CRYPTO-EDGE-001 falsifiability 4/5 (total 58) — the binding obstacle is still a dated per-contract per-event forced-liquidation record covering the post-July-2024 regime, and the vendor's own file-index route contains no liquidation module; CRYPTO-EDGE-003 free-data 5/5 (total 55) — the pair is constructible, the coverage limit is removed, and the remaining obstacle is the untested sign, which free data cannot supply; CRYPTO-EDGE-004 free-data 4/5 (total 48) — access is free and the panel agrees with the published screen to about 0.1% for stable-identifier-matched names, but the free screen's small stratum remains a different population and the published screen's membership remains current-only. The **select-versus-harvest prior was re-verified** from the entry's own source, re-fetched live on 2026-10-21 (HTTP 200, 8,981 bytes): the negative control (a centralised-versus-centralised spread centred on zero with a coin-flip sign, 41-47% stability), the threshold rule at **-9% to -15% annualised after costs** and the unthresholded patient harvest at **+2.7% to +5.4% annualised net** all stand verbatim. The prior is recorded as holding and no re-specification was made to avoid it. **Four candidate families were worked and none was advanced**, and the reasons are recorded so that they are not rediscovered: (i) *a cross-venue funding dispersion on the extended window* — this is CRYPTO-EDGE-003's own registered construction, so it is recorded as a **feasibility result, not a hypothesis**: the two-sided, two-leg filter is executable on 617 dates retrospectively and on 813 dates if the window is extended, and nothing else changes; (ii) *a settlement-aligned cross-venue dispersion* (measuring the dispersion on each instrument's own funding interval rather than on a common 8-hour clock, which the heterogeneous 1h/2h/4h/8h intervals make necessary) — rejected as a new hypothesis because it is a **measurement specification with no registered prediction of its own**: the entry's registered claim is about the *sign* of the venue-relative mapping, and the standing select-versus-harvest prior says the *level* of a market-wide carry spread adds nothing to the harvest; it is recorded as a **specification addition** to the entry, and the new archive is what makes it measurable; (iii) *a dated depth-ladder spread on the second venue* (the newly disclosed 400-level L2 archive, from 2026-06-09) — rejected on two grounds: the depth series is **four months deep**, so it cannot support a registered tail statistic with a pre-registered event count, and a cross-venue liquidity state is a **market-wide** state, so it fails the "not already a proxy" test against the entry's per-contract mechanism; (iv) *a per-contract open-interest level-discontinuity signal on the daily cadence* — rejected on the ground this cycle measured: the per-contract **daily** row's aggregation is undocumented and differs from the aggregate's end-of-window snapshot by **1-2% at the median and up to 23% in the tail**, so any daily-cadence level or change statistic inherits a measurement error of the same order as the effects it would claim to detect, and the select-versus-harvest prior applies to the level as well.
